title: Parlays Push Kalshi Past $3.9 Billion in a Day, Twice in a Weekend
summary: Kalshi set back-to-back daily volume records over the weekend, at $3.91 billion on Saturday and $3.96 billion on Sunday. Parlay-style combos made up about 70% of both days, most of them long shots priced below 1 cent. Combos Supplied Most of the Growth Kalshi’s daily market data, which runs on U.S. ...
content:
Kalshi set back-to-back daily volume records over the weekend, at $3.91 billion on Saturday and $3.96 billion on Sunday. Parlay-style combos made up about 70% of both days, most of them long shots priced below 1 cent.

Key Takeaways

  • Kalshi’s notional volume reached a record $3.91 billion on Saturday and $3.96 billion on Sunday.
  • Combos made up 71.6% of Saturday’s volume and 69.4% of Sunday’s, and most of the weekly growth.

Combos Supplied Most of the Growth

Kalshi’s daily market data, which runs on U.S. Eastern days, shows $3.91 billion in notional volume on Saturday, Oct. 10, and $3.96 billion on Sunday, Oct. 11, both above the previous high of $3.68 billion set on Sunday, Oct. 4. Notional volume counts each contract at its full $1 payout, which the buyer and seller fund between them according to the price.

Both days were about 61% above the corresponding days of the NFL’s opening weekend, when Kalshi set consecutive daily records at under $2.5 billion each. It has now passed $3 billion on seven days, all of them since Sept. 19.

Combos, Kalshi’s parlay-style contracts that bundle several outcomes into one, accounted for $2.80 billion of Saturday’s volume, or 71.6%, and $2.75 billion of Sunday’s, or 69.4%. They also supplied most of the week-over-week growth. Saturday’s total was $459 million higher than on Oct. 3, with combos up $400 million, and Sunday’s was $279 million higher than on Oct. 4, with combos up $218 million.

Much of that combo volume came from long-shot parlays. About 1.9 billion of Saturday’s 2.8 billion combo contracts, and 1.6 billion of Sunday’s 2.75 billion, were in combos whose Yes side never traded at 1 cent or more that day. In those trades, the parlay buyer paid a fraction of a cent per contract and the other side put up the rest of the $1. The rise in those contracts alone accounted for about three-quarters of Saturday’s increase over the previous Saturday and 86% of Sunday’s. One 13-leg combo on NFL winners traded 12.1 million contracts on Sunday at Yes prices between 0.01 cent and 0.44 cent. Parlay buyers paid about $13,800 for them, and the other side put up about $12.1 million. The parlay lost.

Outside combos, college football markets traded $428 million on Saturday, against $17 million for the NFL, which had no games that day. On Sunday, NFL markets traded $572 million, up 18% from a week earlier, and college football $21 million. Kalshi’s 15-minute bitcoin markets traded $229 million on Saturday and $234 million on Sunday, the most of any non-combo series after college football and NFL game markets, respectively.

Separately, Kalshi told the CFTC in a Sept. 28 filing that it would end its Volume Incentive Program no earlier than Oct. 13, nearly a year before its scheduled Oct. 1, 2027, end. The program pays traders a share of per-market rewards, capped at half a cent per contract. For event contracts, only order-book trades at prices between 3 and 97 cents qualify, so the sub-cent combos behind most of the weekend’s growth did not. The filing gave no reason, and it came as the CFTC was reviewing prediction market incentive programs, after an August staff advisory warned that volume-based rewards with steep tiers or threshold bonuses can encourage wash trading.

title: South Korea moves to block 27 crypto websites, including KuCoin, MEXC
summary: Authorities said the restrictions are aimed at unregistered exchanges and have acknowledged that customers could have difficulty withdrawing assets.
content:
South Korean authorities have approved measures to block domestic access to 27 websites operated by unregistered crypto exchanges and other virtual asset service providers, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex and Bitrue. 

In an announcement on Tuesday, South Korea’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) said the decision followed reviews by the Korea Media and Communications Standards Commission on Oct. 6 and 7. 

The list also includes CoinW, BTCC, BitMart, BingX, DigiFinex and others. The block applies to crypto platforms that have not registered under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, the country’s anti-money laundering legislation.

“With this decision, blocking measures against illegal virtual asset operators will also apply to internet websites, following apps such as those on Apple and Google,” the FIU said, according to a translation. 

The measures involve terminating services hosted domestically or blocking access to websites operated overseas. 

The move follows earlier restrictions on mobile apps. Cointelegraph reported in April 2025 that South Korea had blocked downloads and updates for 14 unregistered crypto exchange apps on Apple’s App Store, following restrictions on 17 apps through Google Play.

The FIU said authorities assess whether overseas operators target Korean customers by looking at whether platforms offer Korean-language services, market to South Korean users or support transactions in Korean won. 

The FIU acknowledged the website blocks could complicate withdrawals for existing users. It said it plans to provide withdrawal guidance and support through the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance, or DAXA, with cooperation from the operators. 

Related: South Korea crypto exchange profits fall 78% in H1 amid trading slump

title: Bybit Brings 1,000+ US Stocks and ETFs Into Crypto Trading Accounts
summary: Eligible Bybit users can now trade U.S. equities in the accounts they already use for cryptocurrency trading. The service connects stablecoin balances with underlying securities, extending the platform beyond digital assets into conventional investments. USDC Balances Can Now Buy Apple and Nvidia Sh...
content:
Eligible Bybit users can now trade U.S. equities in the accounts they already use for cryptocurrency trading. The service connects stablecoin balances with underlying securities, extending the platform beyond digital assets into conventional investments.

Key Takeaways

  • Eligible users can purchase stocks with USDC without trading commissions.
  • Fractional shares and extended trading hours are available on eligible securities.
  • Cash dividends arrive in USDC; voting rights are planned for a later phase.

USDC Balances Can Now Buy Apple and Nvidia Shares

Eligible cryptocurrency traders can now buy more than 1,000 U.S.-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds through their existing Bybit accounts. The crypto exchange announced its stock trading expansion on Oct. 12, giving investors access to conventional securities through its USDC-funded stock offering. Access requires completed identity verification and eligibility in a permitted jurisdiction.

Bybit co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou linked the expansion to the company’s effort to combine financial markets within one platform. Zhou said:

“With stocks now available through Bybit, we are doing more than adding another asset class. We are giving people broader access to financial markets and greater freedom to pursue opportunities.”

The initial lineup includes Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL), Nvidia Corp. (Nasdaq: NVDA), Tesla Inc. (Nasdaq: TSLA), and Micron Technology Inc. (Nasdaq: MU). The Invesco QQQ ETF (Nasdaq: QQQ) is also supported. Exchange-traded funds are investment funds whose shares trade on exchanges, and fractional purchases let eligible investors acquire less than one full share of supported securities.

Stock Dividends Return to Accounts as USDC

Purchases provide an economic interest in underlying securities, with brokerage execution and custody handled separately from the exchange interface. Through its partnership with Alpaca, Bybit offers the service via Infra Capital Limited, an introducing broker regulated by Mauritius’ Financial Services Commission. Alpaca Securities LLC, a U.S. broker-dealer, executes orders and holds the assets.

USDC funds purchases as a stablecoin designed to track the U.S. dollar, linking cryptocurrency balances with conventional investments. Such dollar-linked stablecoins target a relatively steady value. Eligible crypto and equity positions can be managed through Bybit’s Unified Trading Account, an account interface that brings these holdings together under one login.

Cash dividends are converted from U.S. dollars into USDC and credited to the holder’s account, subject to applicable terms. Stock dividends appear directly in positions, while stock splits adjust holdings to reflect the corporate action. Eligible purchases and sales carry no trading commissions.

The announced service supports trading 24 hours a day, five days a week, commonly described as 24/5 trading. Availability depends on the product, with access across U.S. premarket, regular, and after-hours sessions. Voting rights are planned for a future phase.

Bybit Builds on Stock Derivatives as Rivals Expand

The launch builds on Bybit’s earlier move into traditional markets, where users already had access to stock derivatives. Its traditional-market integration brought stock contracts for difference, foreign exchange, and commodities into the app in 2025. Those contracts track price changes and are available through Metatrader 5 (MT5), software used to trade traditional-market instruments.

Conventional securities have also entered other cryptocurrency platforms, with exchanges extending their offerings beyond digital assets to include familiar investments. Kraken began commission-free trading in more than 11,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs in April 2025, initially covering selected U.S. jurisdictions. That rollout similarly included fractional purchases and the ability to manage several asset classes within one platform.

Crypto exchange Coinbase (Nasdaq: COIN) and Binance also offer conventional stock trading, with different eligibility rules and funding arrangements across their platforms. Coinbase provides U.S. stocks and ETFs to eligible U.S. residents through Coinbase Capital Markets. Binance launched access to more than 7,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs on June 1 for eligible users, with purchases primarily funded in USDC and fractional shares starting at $5.

Crypto.com and Gemini have likewise incorporated brokerage services into their cryptocurrency platforms, while Robinhood combines both asset classes in its U.S. app. Crypto.com offers more than 12,000 stocks and ETFs to U.S. customers. Gemini’s securities service is available only to eligible U.S. residents in states where it has launched. Robinhood separately offers Classic Stock Tokens in Europe, structured as derivative contracts.

Tokenized equities use blockchain tokens backed by stocks or ETF shares held in custody; xStocks is a brand of these instruments. Kraken’s expanded Alpaca partnership for xStocks designated the broker as a source and custodian for equities backing those tokens. Bybit continues to offer tokenized equities, MT5-based products, and traditional-finance perpetual contracts alongside its new stock service.

title: Meta claims new Muse Wonder AI models rival OpenAI, Anthropic
summary: Meta co-founder Mark Zuckerberg said its newest models are a step toward “personal superintelligence.”
content:
Meta has unveiled two new artificial intelligence models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, which it called its most capable models to date and a step toward “personal superintelligence.”

Meta on Monday said the models introduce two capabilities Meta calls Active Memory and Active Focus. The first carries relevant information across conversations, and the second helps the agent sustain work on difficult tasks.

Independent evaluation platform Artificial Analysis scored Wonder Full at 56 on its Intelligence Index and the standard Wonder at 52, both at maximum reasoning effort.

That puts Full above Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, which each scored 53, but below Claude Opus 5.5’s 58.

Bindu Reddy, CEO of Abacus.AI, which conducts its own model evaluations, challenged the performance claims, writing on X that Muse Wonder was “nowhere near Fable or Astra level” and said detailed benchmark results would follow.

Meta’s new models are its most expensive to date, with the standard Wonder model charging $4 per million input tokens, matching Claude Opus 5.5 but undercutting GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, which charge $10 and $50 respectively.

Wonder Full is available only to people who subscribe to Muse Code’s $50 a month “power usage” or $200 a month “maximum usage” tiers.

Related: Global watchdog flags stablecoin risks, AI threats ahead of G20

title: Ripple’s RLUSD Gains Standard Chartered Custody on the XRP Ledger
summary: Eligible institutions can now safeguard Ripple’s RLUSD on the XRP Ledger through Standard Chartered’s digital asset custody service. The launch expands bank-based stablecoin infrastructure, with a planned LMAX integration targeting future use as trading collateral. Standard Chartered Opens Bank Cust...
content:
Eligible institutions can now safeguard Ripple’s RLUSD on the XRP Ledger through Standard Chartered’s digital asset custody service. The launch expands bank-based stablecoin infrastructure, with a planned LMAX integration targeting future use as trading collateral.

Key Takeaways

  • Standard Chartered’s custody service supports RLUSD on the XRP Ledger.
  • Planned collateral mirroring would keep tokens off the trading venue.
  • Implementation still requires testing, documentation, and approvals.

Standard Chartered Opens Bank Custody for RLUSD

Eligible institutions can now place Ripple USD (RLUSD) issued on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) in Standard Chartered’s custody. The bank announced on Oct. 12 that its institutional RLUSD custody service is live, giving them access to its digital asset infrastructure. Custody involves safeguarding assets on behalf of their owners; the XRPL is a public blockchain supporting financial transactions.

The newly supported asset is Ripple’s dollar-backed token, which belongs to a category of digital assets designed to maintain a stable value. Such stablecoins track assets such as the U.S. dollar. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said:

“RLUSD was built for exactly this kind of institutional use case. Our customers want the efficiency of a regulated stablecoin without giving up the custody standards they already trust.”

The bank provides the RLUSD custody offering through its Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) branch, which is regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA). The launch combines Standard Chartered’s safekeeping capabilities with Ripple’s stablecoin, establishing the custody component of a broader collaboration involving institutional trading infrastructure operator LMAX Group.

The Tokens Stay Put While Their Value Supports Trading

A separate planned integration would make RLUSD eligible collateral, an asset pledged to secure financial obligations, for agreed LMAX products and services. The proposed collateral mirroring model would reflect the value of eligible holdings at LMAX without requiring institutions to transfer the underlying RLUSD directly to the trading venue. Standard Chartered would provide custody, while LMAX would recognize the mirrored collateral value for agreed products and services. LMAX operates institutional trading infrastructure for foreign exchange and digital assets.

The companies expect the structure to reduce operational risks associated with transfers and improve how institutions manage exposure to counterparties, the other parties in financial transactions. They also anticipate greater capital efficiency, allowing eligible holdings to support trading while remaining within the bank’s custody framework. Those benefits depend on successful implementation of the planned capabilities.

The collaboration builds on a multiyear Ripple-LMAX partnership involving $150 million in financing announced Jan. 15. Under that agreement, Ripple committed to provide financing for LMAX’s growth strategy, while LMAX planned to integrate RLUSD as a core collateral asset. The earlier arrangement covered several trading products; the new initiative extends the bank’s collateral mirroring model to LMAX.

Bank Custody Expands, With Implementation Still Ahead

The RLUSD launch extends a custody business that Standard Chartered established in the United Arab Emirates in September 2024. Its initial service supported bitcoin and ether, with Brevan Howard Digital, the crypto and digital asset division of investment manager Brevan Howard, as the inaugural customer. Adding custody for RLUSD broadens the range of assets institutions can safeguard through the bank’s digital asset infrastructure.

Ripple has also developed banking relationships involving the reserves that support its stablecoin’s dollar value, a separate custody function. In July 2025, it selected BNY as RLUSD’s primary reserve custodian. Reserve custody concerns the backing assets, while Standard Chartered’s new offering safeguards eligible institutions’ RLUSD tokens issued on the XRP Ledger.

The issuer’s regulatory structure provides another layer of oversight alongside the arrangements for safeguarding tokens and backing assets. RLUSD’s New York trust charter and reserve safeguards include issuance through Ripple subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company, supervision by the New York Department of Financial Services, segregated reserves, and independent attestations examining reserve disclosures.

The future collateral capabilities remain subject to final documentation, successful testing, applicable laws and regulations, internal approvals, and jurisdictional readiness. The parties will announce further details as implementation progresses.

title: Aptos rolls out Encrypted Mempool to curb frontrunning, sandwich attacks
summary: The optional feature hides transaction details until their order is finalized, preventing bots from exploiting pending trades.
content:
Layer-1 blockchain Aptos has launched an optional new feature that could help shield traders from attacks involving maximal extractable value (MEV), including frontrunning and sandwich attacks. 

On Monday, Aptos said its Encrypted Mempool feature is now live on its mainnet, allowing users to opt in to keep pending transactions encrypted until their block ordering is finalized. Aptos said the feature was built for institutions submitting large transactions to the chain, traders wanting to avoid MEV risk, AI agents and builders. 

“When you send a transaction on any major chain today, anyone watching the network can see the details before it executes, the function you’re calling, the assets and amounts involved, and the contracts you’re interacting with,” Aptos said. “Bots use that visibility to trade against you or copy your strategy.”  

Sandwich attacks, one form of MEV attack, cost Ethereum traders about $60 million over the 12 months through October 2025, according to Cointelegraph’s analysis of EigenPhi data. On Solana, sandwich attacks generated $29.7 million for bots over an 11-month period examined by Bitquery, which identified nearly 6.9 million attacks affecting about 2.2 million wallets. 

How Encrypted Mempool works 

When a user opts in, a compatible wallet or app encrypts the transaction’s contents on their device before sending it to Aptos. Details such as the assets and amounts involved stay hidden, while the sender’s address and gas fee remain visible. 

The encrypted transaction enters the mempool, which is where pending transactions wait to be included in a block. Validators agree on the order of the transactions while being blind to their contents. 

Related: Aptos commits $50M to AI agent infrastructure push

Once the ordering is finalized, validators collectively decrypt the transactions, which are then executed and recorded onchain. No single validator can decrypt a pending transaction on its own. 

Keeping transaction details hidden until their ordering is fixed can prevent bots from reading pending orders and inserting trades ahead or around them to profit at users’ expense. 

The protection comes with added costs and a small delay. Encrypted transactions carry a minimum gas price at twice the network’s base minimum, according to Aptos’ developer documentation. Aptos also said the system adds around 20 milliseconds per block in tests involving 50 nodes, compared to the existing consensus implementation. 

Aptos joins other networks offering protection against harmful MEV. Gnosis Chain launched an encrypted mempool using Shutter in July 2024, while Ethereum’s Flashbots Protect routes transactions privately to block builders. Aptos said its distinction is that its existing validators handle both transaction ordering and decryption, rather than relying on a separate decryption committee or trusted builders.

title: Evernorth Hits Nasdaq With 473 Million XRP as XRPN Trading Begins
summary: Evernorth began Nasdaq trading today, giving stock market investors access to a company built around an actively managed XRP treasury. The listing brings approximately 473 million XRP into a publicly traded business pursuing strategies to increase its cryptocurrency holdings per share. XRPN Starts T...
content:
Evernorth began Nasdaq trading today, giving stock market investors access to a company built around an actively managed XRP treasury. The listing brings approximately 473 million XRP into a publicly traded business pursuing strategies to increase its cryptocurrency holdings per share.

Key Takeaways

  • XRPN reached $17.37, up 2.72% after hours, at 7:30 p.m. EDT.
  • Evernorth entered public markets holding approximately 473 million XRP.
  • Management plans to deploy capital and increase XRP held per share.

XRPN Starts Trading as XRP Treasury Reaches Nasdaq

Stock market investors gained access to Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) on Oct. 12 as the XRP treasury company’s shares opened for trading. Its start of Nasdaq trading follows the completion of a merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, a special purpose acquisition company formed to bring another business public. XRPN identifies Evernorth’s common stock.

Shares finished the regular session at $16.91, down 18 cents, or 1.05%, from the previous close. By 7:30 p.m. EDT, XRPN’s after-hours price stood at $17.37, up 46 cents, or 2.72%, from the session’s closing level, according to Nasdaq data captured that evening.

The launch followed an administrative delay that moved the planned market debut four days beyond its original target. The revised merger and trading timetable replaced an Oct. 7 closing and Oct. 8 trading start with Oct. 9 and Oct. 12, respectively. Armada shareholders had approved the transaction at their Sept. 30 meeting.

473 Million XRP Backs an Active Treasury Strategy

Evernorth held approximately 473 million XRP at closing and had raised approximately $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. Its completed XRP treasury merger brought together financing and institutional backing from investors including Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, and GSR.

Founder and Chief Executive Officer Asheesh Birla outlined the operating strategy in the company’s Oct. 9 business combination announcement. He said:

“Completing this transaction today marks a significant milestone of bringing this company to market.”

Evernorth intends to pursue institutional and decentralized finance yield strategies, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities to increase XRP per share.

That objective measures the quantity of tokens held relative to outstanding shares, linking treasury growth to the number of outstanding shares. Purchasing Evernorth shares gives investors an ownership interest in the business. Holding cryptocurrency directly instead means owning the digital asset itself. The equity investment combines XRP exposure with Evernorth’s financing structure, operating decisions, and business performance.

The transaction’s financing details show substantial shareholder redemptions before the combined business reached public markets. Holders redeemed approximately 80.3% of Armada shares eligible for redemption, receiving about $195.39 million in cash, the SEC filing states. Separately, Evernorth identifies tokenized assets, blockchain-based credit markets, and settlement infrastructure as potential areas for capital deployment.

Evernorth Sets Nasdaq Bell Ceremony for Oct. 14

The debut week also extends Evernorth’s public campaign recognizing supporters who remained involved in the XRP ecosystem through setbacks. Its XRP community campaign features Bearchamp, a boxing bear character created by Chicago artist JC Rivera. The collaboration developed through a series of chapters leading toward a Times Square presentation.

Evernorth expects to ring the Nasdaq closing bell Oct. 14 with company leadership, investors, and XRP ecosystem participants. That afternoon, the final chapter of the Bearchamp collaboration is scheduled to premiere in Times Square, New York, at around 4 p.m. Eastern, the company stated in its Oct. 10 update on X.

title: Bitcoin Price Falls Below $82K as $406M in Longs Get Liquidated
summary: Bitcoin cracked below $82,000 Monday evening, setting off another painful reckoning for leveraged crypto traders. Nearly $489 million in positions vanished over 24 hours, with bullish bets accounting for more than 83% of the damage as the broader market stumbled. Bitcoin’s Slide Wipes Out 118,000 Cr...
content:
Bitcoin cracked below $82,000 Monday evening, setting off another painful reckoning for leveraged crypto traders. Nearly $489 million in positions vanished over 24 hours, with bullish bets accounting for more than 83% of the damage as the broader market stumbled.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell below $82,000 Monday as $488.61 million in crypto liquidations hit 118,142 traders.
  • Coinglass data shows bullish positions accounted for $406.48 million, or 83.2%, of liquidations.
  • Ethereum, solana and XRP joined bitcoin’s decline as investors awaited Wednesday’s CPI report.

Bitcoin’s Slide Wipes Out 118,000 Crypto Traders

On Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, bitcoin’s price slipped below the $82,000 threshold, extending a decline that had dragged the cryptocurrency down from an earlier high near $84,254. By approximately 7:30 p.m. Eastern time, Coinglass liquidation figures showed $488.61 million in leveraged crypto positions had been wiped out over 24 hours.

The damage reached 118,142 traders, with long positions accounting for $406.48 million and shorts contributing $82.14 million. Put differently, more than $83 of every $100 liquidated came from traders betting on higher prices. Ethereum led individual assets with $115.19 million in liquidations, followed by bitcoin at $106.61 million.

Source: Coinglass, Oct. 12, 2026, 7:30 p.m. Eastern time.

The crypto asset solana (SOL) contributed another $26.97 million, while zcash and NEAR registered approximately $19.86 million and $19.81 million, respectively. Binance accounted for 52.3% of the total. The largest individual liquidation was a $9.65 million bitcoin long position on Binance, executed at $81,772.

Four Factors Driving Bitcoin’s Latest Decline

Bitcoin’s retreat below $82,000 appears to reflect five overlapping pressures, ranging from institutional withdrawals to macroeconomic uncertainty and a fresh wave of leveraged liquidations.

1. Spot bitcoin ETF Outflows: U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded approximately $679 million to $681 million in net outflows during the Oct. 5-9 trading week. The withdrawals weakened a source of institutional demand that had previously helped support bitcoin’s price.

2. Elevated Treasury Yields: The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed toward 5.24% to 5.3%, making interest-bearing assets more attractive relative to bitcoin. Higher borrowing costs and expectations of restrictive Federal Reserve policy have also weighed on investors’ appetite for risk.

3. Rising Oil Prices and Geopolitical Tensions: Elevated crude oil prices, fueled partly by renewed Middle East tensions, have complicated the inflation outlook. Higher energy costs threaten to keep consumer prices elevated, potentially limiting the Federal Reserve’s flexibility on interest rates.

4. Inflation Anxiety and Technical Weakness: Investors are approaching Wednesday’s consumer price index (CPI) report cautiously, with producer price index (PPI) data scheduled for Thursday. Meanwhile, bitcoin’s repeated failure to reclaim the $84,000 to $87,000 range has shifted attention toward support between $81,000 and $82,000.

Together, these pressures have left bitcoin’s price struggling to regain momentum. Wednesday’s inflation figures could determine whether the latest retreat remains contained within its established trading range or develops into a deeper correction.

Ethereum, Solana and XRP Join the Retreat

Bitcoin wasn’t alone. Ethereum’s price traded near $2,461, down 2.79% over 24 hours and 9.34% over seven days. SOL changed hands around $106.16, losing 4.39% daily and 12.09% weekly. XRP declined 4.33% to $1.34, while dogecoin (DOGE) slipped 4.02% to approximately $0.08311.

Hyperliquid (HYPE) and zcash (ZEC) suffered even steeper daily declines of 5.44% and 5.82%, respectively. Attention now turns to Wednesday’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI) report, scheduled for Oct. 14, followed by producer price data on Thursday.

With bitcoin struggling to reclaim $84,000 and support being tested between $81,000 and $82,000, traders face an uncomfortable question. Has the market cleared enough leverage to stabilize, or will inflation data deliver another round of forced liquidations?

title: Sydney Sweeney Mocks Bets on Her Underwear and Dictator Deaths in New Novig Ad
summary: Sydney Sweeney is back in a new ad for Novig. The 30-second spot for the sports-only prediction market keeps the “just sports” slogan from the September launch ad, but this time takes aim at insider trading, bots, and war bets elsewhere in the industry. A Sports-Only Pitch Aimed at Rivals’ Other Mar...
content:
Sydney Sweeney is back in a new ad for Novig. The 30-second spot for the sports-only prediction market keeps the “just sports” slogan from the September launch ad, but this time takes aim at insider trading, bots, and war bets elsewhere in the industry.

Key Takeaways

  • Sydney Sweeney’s new Novig ad mocks insider trading on “dictators dying” and bets on war.
  • Novig posted the 30-second spot on Oct. 11, a month after its Sept. 9 launch ad drew athletes’ criticism.

A Sports-Only Pitch Aimed at Rivals’ Other Markets

Novig posted the 30-second ad on X on Sunday, Oct. 11, with the caption “No dictators. No market manipulation. No insider trading. No BS. Just sports.” Sweeney, who joined the company as an equity holder, appears topless again and opens with a joke about the markets themselves: “There are grown men making spreadsheets to bet on what color underwear I’m wearing. I mean, I’m flattered?”

The spot then turns on the rest of the industry. “There’s insider trading on dictators dying and armies of bots manipulating it all. There’s someone sitting in a bathroom stall betting their 401(k) on a war,” Sweeney says, before contrasting those markets with “people who just trade on sports.” She names no competitors, though Kalshi and Polymarket, the two biggest platforms in the sector, both run markets on elections and world events as well as games.

Insider trading claims have dogged the sector: Kalshi is investigating suspicious trades tied to President Donald Trump’s pick of Katie Zacharia as White House press secretary, including at least three small bets placed before news of her selection emerged, among them a $19 wager set to pay $1,896, The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct. 9, citing a company spokesperson. In April, the Justice Department charged a U.S. soldier with using classified information about the operation to capture Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro to make more than $400,000 on Polymarket.

The new spot builds on the campaign’s Sept. 9 launch ad, in which Sweeney posed nude behind sports equipment and promised “no betting on wars or deaths, and no politics.” That ad drew criticism from female athletes, including Australian Olympic swimming champion Ariarne Titmus, who said it sexualized women’s sport. Sweeney’s “Euphoria” co-star Sharon Stone told People it was up to Sweeney “to take responsibility for her actions” but not up to Stone to judge her, adding: “We can’t denigrate women’s sports to get men’s attention so they can gamble.”

Novig says the launch ad paid off. Co-founder and CEO Jacob Fortinsky said earlier this month that trading volume rose nearly 94% in the 20 days before and after the campaign launched, though that window also included the start of the NFL season.

title: Moscow Exchange to Launch Bitcoin Trading, Testing Underway
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Moscow Exchange to Launch Bitcoin Trading, Testing Underway
Russia in recent months has paved the way to allow its citizens to trade bitcoin. 
This post Moscow Exchange to Launch Bitcoin Trading, Testing Underway first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
The Moscow Exchange plans to let clients trade cryptocurrencies starting in December and has begun testing operations with professional market participants, a senior executive said last week.

“We are actively testing. We started a week ago,” Boris Blokhin, the exchange’s senior managing director for sales and business development, told journalists on the sidelines of the Sber Investments forum, according to a Thursday Interfax report. 

The exchange — the biggest in Russia — will work with a partner settlement digital depository, where market participants will open accounts. It won’t need any additional permits or licenses to launch trading, Blokhin added.

The plan follows Russia’s law on digital currencies and digital rights, which took effect in September and sets comprehensive rules for crypto in the country. 

Trades can run through existing infrastructure such as exchanges, brokers and trust managers. New players will also join, including crypto exchangers, where assets are bought and sold, and digital depositories, which record ownership.

Russia’s largest bank, Sberbank, announced last month it was the first in the country to have been approved to custody bitcoin. The Bank of Russia gave it the green light for “digital currency record-keeping” and to facilitate the transfer of such assets, covering bitcoin and other, smaller cryptocurrencies.

Russia’s relationship with Bitcoin is complicated. President Vladimir Putin in 2024 seemed to praise the original cryptocurrency back in 2024. “For example, Bitcoin, who can ban it? Nobody,” he said at a forum at the time. 

But the Kremlin keeps a tight grip on what citizens can do with it. Using crypto as a form of payment has been illegal in Russia since 2022; unqualified investors can buy bitcoin and stablecoins capped at 300,000 rubles ($3,556) a year through a single intermediary. 

Qualified investors can buy any cryptocurrency traded on exchange and over-the-counter markets, with no limit.

President Putin in October signed a law to set in stone the regulation of digital currencies and digital rights in the country.  

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: South Korean Lender Jeonbuk Bank to Offer Bitcoin-Backed Loans
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korean Lender Jeonbuk Bank to Offer Bitcoin-Backed Loans
The South Korean bank has become the first in the country to offer the bitcoin-related service. 
This post South Korean Lender Jeonbuk Bank to Offer Bitcoin-Backed Loans first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written...
content:
Jeonbuk Bank has become the first bank in South Korea to offer won-denominated loans backed by bitcoin, according to reports. 

The subsidiary of JB Financial Group has started offering the loans, according to exclusive Monday reporting by the country’s Edaily paper. 

For now, the product is limited to corporate customers raising working capital, and bitcoin is the only eligible collateral. The bank said it may expand the service depending on regulatory changes and market demand, the report added. 

Jeonbuk Bank won’t own or control the bitcoin itself. The collateral is held by a specialized custodian, limited to virtual asset service providers registered under Korea’s Act on the Reporting of Specific Financial Information, it further noted. 

If a borrower defaults, the bank won’t take the coins but will rather liquidate them through enforcement procedures such as a court-ordered sale and recover the loan from the proceeds.

The bank said it chose bitcoin for its market capitalization and trading volume, the largest of any digital asset, and that its own stress tests showed bitcoin held up as collateral even during sharp price declines. To value the collateral, it uses an index based on a weighted average of prices across multiple global exchanges.

Similar products already exist abroad. JPMorgan Chase debuted bitcoin-backed loans for institutional clients in March, and Switzerland’s Sygnum Bank offers comparable credit.

The loan is the first concrete result of the “Crypto Bank” vision put forward by Jeonbuk Bank President Park Chun-won. The lender is the only regional bank to provide real-name verified accounts to crypto exchanges, and it is preparing an “all-in-one wallet” that combines fiat accounts and digital asset wallets.

“This loan is an example of designing a risk management and recovery structure that allows us to utilize existing bank lending and collateral management systems without directly holding virtual assets,” said Jeong Sang-hoon, executive vice president of the bank’s digital division.

title: South Korea’s Bitcoin Lending Experiment Begins at Jeonbuk Bank
summary: South Korea just cracked open the door to bitcoin-backed banking, according to local reports. Jeonbuk Bank has executed the country’s first reported traditional bank loan secured by bitcoin, allowing businesses to borrow Korean won without selling their coins or surrendering ownership to the lender....
content:
South Korea just cracked open the door to bitcoin-backed banking, according to local reports. Jeonbuk Bank has executed the country’s first reported traditional bank loan secured by bitcoin, allowing businesses to borrow Korean won without selling their coins or surrendering ownership to the lender.

Key Takeaways

  • Edaily and Maeil Business Newspaper detailed that Jeonbuk Bank has executed South Korea’s first reported traditional bank loan secured by bitcoin.
  • New rules effective Oct. 1 let Jeonbuk Bank pursue court-supervised collateral recovery without holding bitcoin.
  • Jeonbuk Bank limits the arrangement to corporate borrowers, with rates and collateral requirements undisclosed.

A Bitcoin Loan Without Touching Bitcoin

Jeonbuk Bank, a subsidiary of JB Financial Group, has introduced a restricted corporate lending arrangement that accepts bitcoin as collateral while keeping the cryptocurrency entirely outside the bank’s custody. The news was first reported in an exclusive by the regional publication Edaily, and reporter Lee Jeong Hun.

Instead, licensed third-party custodians safeguard the pledged bitcoin, while Jeonbuk Bank handles credit assessments, collateral valuations, and loan issuance. The arrangement is limited to corporate working capital, including payroll, supplier payments, and everyday operating expenses. Individual borrowers are excluded, and the digital asset bitcoin (BTC) remains the only accepted cryptocurrency.

Korean media differ slightly on the rollout. Edaily describes a limited service launch, while Maeil Business Newspaper characterizes the transaction as a pilot involving an existing corporate loan.

New Court Rules Open the Door

The real breakthrough centers on what happens when a borrower defaults. Under revised Civil Enforcement Rules effective Oct. 1, 2026, Jeonbuk Bank can pursue court-supervised recovery without ever taking possession of the pledged bitcoin. A court-ordered sale would liquidate the collateral, with proceeds applied toward the outstanding debt.

This structure allows the bank to operate within existing lending regulations while avoiding direct cryptocurrency custody. Custodians must satisfy South Korea’s regulatory requirements, including registration, security certification, segregated asset protection and applicable cold-storage obligations.

Bitcoin Gets the Green Light

Jeonbuk Bank selected bitcoin because of its substantial market capitalization, trading liquidity and established price discovery. The lender reportedly conducted internal stress tests examining bitcoin’s suitability as collateral during steep market declines.

It also developed a digital-asset valuation framework combining weighted prices from multiple international exchanges with volatility indicators to minimize pricing distortions. However, the South Korean bank has kept several important details under wraps. Interest rates, loan-to-value ratios, liquidation thresholds, loan amounts and the borrower’s identity have not been publicly disclosed.

A New Chapter for Korean Banking

The transaction represents a tangible development in South Korea’s efforts to incorporate digital assets into traditional finance (TradFi) services. Jeonbuk Bank has previously explored blockchain payments, settlements, remittances and stablecoins. It is also developing an integrated wallet connecting traditional bank accounts with digital assets.

The lender plans to refine its monitoring and recovery procedures before considering additional cryptocurrencies or broader lending purposes. For corporate bitcoin holders, the proposition is simple. They can unlock Korean won liquidity without immediately liquidating their holdings.

Still, with commercial terms undisclosed and access restricted to businesses, South Korea’s bitcoin-backed banking experiment has cleared its first hurdle without revealing how far the country’s lenders are prepared to go.

title: FTX’s crypto mining venture is now used to advance AI
summary: The defunct exchange acquired a 20% stake in Genesis Digital Assets before FTX declared bankruptcy in November 2022.
content:
The investment company SWI Group has raised about $900 million in capital as part of plans to scale its data center and AI computing capacity, which includes a mining operation previously tied to cryptocurrency exchange FTX.

In a Monday notice, SWI Group said the 800-million-euro, or about $900 million, capital raise would fund its AI and data center expansion plans in Europe and the United States. The group reportedly now has majority control over one of FTX’s mining companies, Genesis Digital Assets, which will be a part of the network of data centers’ computing capacity.

SWI announced in June that it had acquired “significant shareholding” in Genesis for $500 million. At the time, the company reported that Genesis had 15 facilities with 1.3 gigawatts of capacity. The firm said that it held a 70% stake in Genesis as of August, allowing it to rename the mining venture to SWI Digital.

The acquisition of Genesis, one of the assets embroiled in FTX’s downfall, came as the debtors behind the crypto exchange’s bankruptcy proceedings sought to claw back funds. Former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried reportedly directed the exchange’s sister firm, Alameda Research, to spend more than $1 billion to buy a 20% stake in Genesis between 2021 and 2022. 

FTX filed for bankruptcy in November 2022, leading to criminal charges for many executives over the misuse of customer funds. SWI’s co-founder and CEO Max-Hervé George reportedly said all the legal disputes related to FTX’s stake in Genesis had been resolved.

title: SWI Turns FTX’s Former Bitcoin Mining Infrastructure Toward AI Boom
summary: Genesis Digital Assets, once one of Sam Bankman-Fried’s largest crypto investments, is being repurposed for the artificial-intelligence boom after SWI Group took majority control. SWI has now raised about $896 million to expand the former bitcoin miner’s data-center footprint for hyperscale computin...
content:
Genesis Digital Assets, once one of Sam Bankman-Fried’s largest crypto investments, is being repurposed for the artificial-intelligence boom after SWI Group took majority control. SWI has now raised about $896 million to expand the former bitcoin miner’s data-center footprint for hyperscale computing customers.

Key Takeaways

  • SWI Group took control of Genesis Digital and raised about $896M to expand AI data centers.
  • The pivot shows bitcoin miners are repurposing power infrastructure for higher-value AI compute.
  • The key test is whether SWI can turn former mining sites into durable hyperscale contracts.

Genesis Digital Pivots From Bitcoin Mining to AI Data Centers

A bitcoin mining company once tangled in the wreckage of FTX is getting a second life, this time as an artificial-intelligence (AI) infrastructure play.

SWI Group has acquired a majority stake in Genesis Digital Assets and plans to convert much of its data-center estate from crypto mining toward AI and cloud-computing workloads, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The Amsterdam-listed infrastructure company announced on Monday, Oct. 12, that it has raised $896 million (€800 million) to finance upgrades and expansion across its data-center portfolio.

“We need capital to deploy more compute,” SWI Chief Executive Max-Hervé George said. On bitcoin mining, his position was even clearer: he has “zero interest.”

From Bitcoin Mining to AI Compute

The assets SWI wants are the power-heavy data centers Genesis Digital built across Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Sweden.

Those facilities could now be repurposed for hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, which need enormous amounts of computing capacity to support AI services.

Genesis Digital previously focused heavily on bitcoin mining, including large operations in Kazakhstan. SWI is now selling the company’s final three small mining sites there.

The pivot reflects a broader trend across crypto mining. Data-center operators that once optimized facilities for bitcoin are increasingly chasing AI customers, where long-term computing contracts can offer more predictable and potentially higher returns.

FTX Put More Than $1 Billion Into Genesis Digital

Genesis Digital’s history makes the turnaround particularly striking.

Founded in 2017, the company grew into one of the world’s largest bitcoin miners. Alameda Research, the trading firm closely linked to FTX, began investing in 2021 and ultimately spent more than $1 billion, acquiring roughly a 20% stake.

After FTX collapsed in November 2022, bankruptcy administrators later described Genesis Digital as one of Bankman-Fried’s most reckless investments. They sued to recover about $1.15 billion, arguing that some of the miner’s assets had been dramatically overvalued.

The lawsuit was dropped on June 15, 2026.

SWI Bets $500 Million, Then Takes Control

The same day the lawsuit was dropped, SWI announced an initial $500 million investment in Genesis Digital. It has since increased its stake to become the majority owner. George said disputes involving FTX and other shareholders have now been settled.

For SWI, the acquisition is less about reviving a crypto miner than buying scarce power infrastructure already built for energy-intensive computing.

That is what makes the deal worth watching.

Genesis Digital was once a symbol of excess during the crypto boom. Now its most valuable asset may be something entirely different: data centers that can be rewired for the AI economy.

title: Bitcoin Extends Slide — Can ‘Uptober’ 2026 Beat Last Year’s?
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Extends Slide — Can ‘Uptober’ 2026 Beat Last Year’s?
Bitcoin is off to a rough start so far this month. But things could still turn around. 
This post Bitcoin Extends Slide — Can ‘Uptober’ 2026 Beat Last Year’s? first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di...
content:
Bitcoin’s price dipped further on Monday, sliding 2% over a 24-hour period to trade at a little over $82,423. 

The coin over the past week has dropped by 3%, and so far this month, it’s trading down. 

October is usually a strong month for the OG cryptocurrency. Data from Coinglass shows that it has finished eight of the last 10 Octobers in the green. 

Last year was one of the exceptions: while bitcoin’s price notched an all-time high of $126,080, it then started to enter a bear market after October 10 — when the biggest crypto liquidation event in history battered the asset’s price. 

Markets across the board got hit hard following tariff threats from U.S. President Donald Trump. Crypto long positions got wiped out and over $19 billion in digital asset bets were liquidated. 

Bitcoin then spent most of 2026 in a bear market. 

The good news? That the coin just had its best quarter in years and a good September — historically a rough month for the cryptocurrency. Analysts now are saying that while it’s got off to a bad start so far in “Uptober”, signs of a bottom this month may already be in. 

Writing for data firm CryptoQuant, Japanese asset management platform XWIN said it could be up from here. 

“Now, signs of a potential bottom are emerging,” XWIN said in a note. “On October 12, markets priced roughly an 18% chance of an October Fed hike, while Brent crude had eased from nearly $110 to around $103.”

It added: “‘Uptober’ need not mean uninterrupted gains: a correction can build the foundation for the next advance.”

High oil prices have — at least in the short-term — hurt bitcoin’s price as investors then expect the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates in order to control inflation. 

But while the U.S. central bank last month raised interest rates, bitcoin’s price was unfazed and rose following the news. 

Other analysts have now said the biggest cryptocurrency is out of a bear market due to it crossing its 365-day moving average — a signal that has marked the start of its bull markets in past cycles.

Mathew Di Salvo

title: “Bring Your Portfolio Home”: Robinhood and Rivals Target Webull Clients after China Scrutiny
summary:
Robinhood, SoFi and Public are using the scrutiny surrounding Webull to compete for its customer assets. All three launched Webull-specific transfer incentives after a bipartisan House committee labelled the brokerage’s China ties a national security risk.
The platforms are offering a 3% match on el...
content:
2026-10-12T21:42:41.280+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 19:42 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Robinhood, SoFi and Public are offering 3% matches on eligible portfolio transfers from Webull.
  • The offers use different caps and payout schedules, but require assets to remain for up to six years.

Robinhood, SoFi and Public are using the scrutiny surrounding Webull to compete for its customer assets. All three launched Webull-specific transfer incentives after a bipartisan House committee labelled the brokerage’s China ties a national security risk.

The platforms are offering a 3% match on eligible transfers from Webull through the Automated Customer Account Transfer Service (ACATS). The system allows investors to move eligible securities and cash between US brokerages without selling most transferable holdings.

Robinhood Converts an Existing Promotion into a Webull Offer

Robinhood already had a broader account-transfer campaign offering eligible customers personalised match rates of between 1% and 3%.

It amended the published terms to give transfers originating from Webull a fixed 3% rate from 7 October, regardless of the customer’s personalised offer. The Webull offer runs until 16 October.

The bonus has no stated maximum and is credited once the transferred assets reach the customer’s Robinhood account. However, transferred value must generally remain at Robinhood for five years to avoid a potential proportional chargeback.

Robinhood’s advertising went beyond the usual language of transfer promotions. “American assets should be at America’s favorite broker,” CEO Vlad Tenev wrote on X.

The company separately told Webull users to “bring your portfolio home,” explicitly connecting the incentive to Robinhood’s US identity.

Robinhood is proudly American, founded here to give everyday investors more access to the financial system. If you’re still on Webull, bring your portfolio home and get 3% on your transfer today: https://t.co/QuCN3myHTj

— Robinhood (@RobinhoodApp) October 7, 2026

Public and SoFi Join the Transfer Push

Public created a separate programme for taxable brokerage accounts and IRAs transferred from Webull. The 3% reward applies to transfers initiated by 26 October and is paid in monthly instalments over six years.

The company caps eligible transferred assets at $1 million, producing a maximum match of $30,000.

SoFi is offering the same percentage on Webull transfers into eligible self-directed taxable accounts and IRAs. Its promotion runs from 8 to 15 October and replaces the standard 1% ACATS match available under a separate campaign.

Robinhood is proudly American, founded here to give everyday investors more access to the financial system. If you’re still on Webull, bring your portfolio home and get 3% on your transfer today: https://t.co/QuCN3myHTj

— Robinhood (@RobinhoodApp) October 7, 2026

SoFi caps the reward at $150,000, equivalent to 3% of a $5 million transfer, and requires the assets to remain for five years to retain the full bonus. The offers differ in duration, payment schedule and maximum value, but all three brokers selected the same competitor immediately after the congressional report.

Scrutiny Creates a Commercial Opening

The House committee said Webull remained more closely connected to China than its public positioning suggested. It pointed to the founder’s voting control, the company’s large China-based technology workforce and the possibility that US customer data could be exposed to personnel or laws in the country.

Webull’s shares fell by almost 30% intraday after the report became public.

In a statement filed with the SEC, Webull said the report contained important factual errors. It maintained that US customer data and assets remain in the United States, that China-based employees cannot access sensitive customer information and that the committee identified no misuse of data.

The transfer campaigns provide an early test of whether political scrutiny can move more than a broker’s share price. Because ACATS makes brokerage portfolios portable, Robinhood, SoFi and Public are giving Webull customers a direct financial incentive to turn reputational concerns into actual asset outflows.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, a new report from Stripe-backed blockchain Tempo argues that proposed US accounting rules could remove a major barrier to corporate stablecoin adoption, the Financial Stability Board (FSB) warned G20 officials about stablecoin oversight gaps and AI-related financial risks and XRP Ledger developers defended an emergency security patch that bypassed the network’s usual voting process.

US accounting proposal could clear path for corporate stablecoin adoption

A proposed change to US accounting standards could make it easier for corporations to hold and use stablecoins without compromising their reported cash positions, according to a new report from Stripe-backed blockchain Tempo.

The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) is considering allowing qualifying stablecoins to be classified as cash equivalents on corporate balance sheets. Currently, companies may have to report stablecoin holdings as other assets, which can affect liquidity ratios and compliance with loan covenants.

Tempo said the proposed treatment would depend on whether companies have direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers. This means two companies holding identical USDC tokens could receive different accounting treatment depending on their arrangements with Circle.

For example, Coinbase classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report, supported by its direct redemption arrangement with Circle.

The proposal follows the passage of the GENIUS Act, which established federal requirements for payment stablecoin issuers. FASB’s separate initiative addresses how businesses account for those assets.

The accounting proposal remains open for public comment until Nov. 19.

Global watchdog flags stablecoin risks, AI threats ahead of G20

The FSB, a global financial watchdog, has outlined financial stability risks associated with artificial intelligence and regulatory concerns surrounding stablecoins.

In a letter published Monday, FSB Chair Andrew Bailey warned that cross-border mechanisms for stablecoin oversight and crisis management “remain immature or are not yet developed.” In its 2025 review, the FSB found that 11 of 28 surveyed jurisdictions had finalized stablecoin regulatory frameworks.

He also urged G20 members to support the FSB’s newly finalized practices for responsible AI adoption in the financial sector.

“AI therefore requires our continued close attention alongside careful management by financial institutions,” Bailey wrote.

The FSB submitted the letter to G20 finance ministers and central bank governors ahead of their Thursday meeting. The G20 brings together the world’s major economies to coordinate financial policy and regulatory priorities.

XRP Ledger defends emergency patch for unlimited XRP bug

XRP Ledger developers have defended the emergency security patch used to fix a bug capable of creating XRP beyond the network’s fixed supply, saying they could not wait for the network’s usual two-week validator vote without exposing the flaw to attackers.

The fix, released on Sept. 25, came three days after a bug bounty report, and took effect immediately on any server that installed it. It was the first deliberate bypass of the normal amendment process since the system was introduced more than ten years ago, they said. 

“With a normal amendment vote, the fix would have been public for weeks before it took effect, risking network security,” XRPL developers said in an X post on Sunday. 

The expedited fix led to questions about XRPL’s level of decentralization. On its website, XRPL claims it is a fully decentralized, public blockchain — a characterization that has been central to arguments that its native token, XRP, is not a security.

title: Crypto PACs report $2.7M spending blitz on House races as midterms loom
summary: With just 22 days until the US midterm elections, a crypto-aligned committee has announced another major ad expenditure to support “pro-crypto” candidates in 2026.
content:
Update (Oct. 13, 3:41 am UTC): This article has been updated to reflect that Andreessen Horowitz is one of the contributors funding Fairshake, and not Cantor Fitzgerald.

Affiliate entities of Fairshake, the US political action committee (PAC) funded largely by contributions from Andreessen Horowitz, cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase and Ripple Labs, reported millions of dollars worth of ad buys to support candidates they considered in favor of pro-digital asset policy with the country’s midterm elections less than a month away.

On Saturday, filings with the US Federal Election Commission (FEC) showed a combined $2.7 million in spending on media by the Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress PACs. The two Fairshake affiliates reported expenditures on media and direct mail productions to support Democratic and Republican candidates running for US House of Representatives seats in 2026.

The expenditures included more than $76,000 for House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, $73,000 for House Agriculture Committee Chair Glenn Thompson, $512,000 for California Representative Pete Aguilar and $500,000 for New Jersey Representative Josh Gottheimer. 

The FEC reports followed Fairshake announcing just days earlier that it planned to endorse an additional 32 House candidates in 2026, including six to each receive $1 million in supportive media. None of the aforementioned six were included in the Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress expenditures, but some incumbents were on the list, including Emmer, Aguilar, Gottheimer, and Thompson.

As of August, a Fairshake spokesperson said the PAC had $122 million in cash on hand as part of its midterm election strategy of attempting to get more “pro-crypto” candidates in Congress. This strategy includes opposing the election of former banking committee chair Sherrod Brown in Ohio’s Senate race with at least $30 million allocated for media buys. While in office, Brown was one of the leading Democrats voting against many bills considered favorable to the crypto industry.

Related: Vivek Ramaswamy’s gubernatorial run lacks the crypto rhetoric of his presidential bid

Crypto market structure bill to be a factor in 2026 midterms?

All the targets of the Fairshake spending voted for the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act in 2025, a bill intended to set market structure rules for the cryptocurrency industry, including giving the federal commodities regulator, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, more authority to oversee and enforce regulations. The bill passed the House with bipartisan support but failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate in September.

Stand With Crypto, an initiative launched by Coinbase that ranks lawmakers and politicians based on their public statements and voting records related to the industry, warned after the failed CLARITY vote that candidates who failed to advance legislation could face “consequences” in the midterms. The group is attempting to mobilize crypto-minded US voters in the upcoming election, as it did in 2024 races.

title: US accounting overhaul could make stablecoins more attractive to corporations: Tempo
summary: A Tempo report examines how proposed US accounting rules could change corporate stablecoin holdings, with direct redemption rights determining which tokens qualify as cash.
content:
A new report from Stripe-backed blockchain Tempo argues that a proposed US accounting change could remove a major barrier to corporate stablecoin adoption by allowing qualifying tokens to be classified as cash equivalents on company balance sheets.

The report examines an Accounting Standards Update the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) proposed in August that could make stablecoins more practical for corporate treasury operations. Under current accounting practices, stablecoin holdings may not count toward a company’s reported cash reserves, affecting liquidity ratios and loan covenants even when the tokens are fully backed by dollars.

The proposed change could let companies use stablecoins for payments and settlements without those accounting complications.

According to Tempo, the FASB proposal would require companies to have direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers. For example, buying USDC through an exchange would not necessarily let a company classify those tokens as cash equivalents.

Tempo cites Coinbase, which classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report, supported by its redemption arrangement with Circle.

“Your contract with the issuer is what qualifies, and the token alone doesn’t get you there,” Tempo said.

The FASB proposal remains open for public comment until Nov. 19. The board will review the feedback before finalizing the accounting changes and setting an effective date.

Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t

Stablecoin regulation takes shape in the US

The FASB proposal follows the passage of the GENIUS Act in July 2025, which established the first comprehensive federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins in the United States. The law is scheduled to take effect in January 2027, or 120 days after federal regulators finalize implementing rules, whichever comes first.

While the GENIUS Act establishes requirements for stablecoin issuers, including reserve backing and redemption obligations, the FASB proposal addresses how companies account for stablecoins they hold.

The developments come as the market for US dollar-backed stablecoins has surpassed $300 billion, according to DefiLlama data. The Trump administration is also reportedly exploring ways to promote dollar-backed stablecoins overseas, potentially reinforcing the US dollar’s role as the dominant reserve currency.

According to Bloomberg, the administration is weighing partnerships with private companies to develop stablecoin projects overseas, potentially involving the Treasury Department, State Department and US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).

title: Justin Sun’s $2.25B Crypto Portfolio Includes $1.09B in SUSDS Across 10 Blockchains
summary:

The post Justin Sun’s $2.25B Crypto Portfolio Includes $1.09B in SUSDS Across 10 Blockchains appeare...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Earlier, Arkham reported that it tracks around $2.25 billion worth of on-chain assets for Justin Sun, spanning 10 different blockchain networks.
  • The bulk of the portfolio (around $1.09 billion) is in SUSDS with $607.55 million in STETH and $336.73 million in BTC.
  • In September, Arkham said that its research team had ranked him second to Satoshi Nakamoto, and ranked 211 addresses that were linked to him.

According to blockchain intelligence platform Arkham, Justin Sun, founder of TRON, owns over $2.2 billion in cryptocurrency assets. The data underscore the extent of his positioned estates as well as the share of his wealth maintained in stable coin related and Ethereum associated resources.

  • Arkham Tracks $2.25 Billion Across 10 Chains
  • SUSDS and STETH Dominate Sun’s Portfolio
    • Stablecoin Exposure Stands Out
    • On-Chain Data Offers a Window into Crypto Wealth

Arkham Tracks $2.25 Billion Across 10 Chains

Arkham announced the figures on X, stating that it had labeled approximately $2.25 billion in wallets linked to Sun across 10 blockchain networks. Its dashboard displays a portfolio value of around $2.246 billion and identifies 211 associated addresses.

JUSTIN SUN HOLDS $2.2 BILLION ON-CHAIN

Arkham has labelled $2.25B of Justin Sun’s wallets across 10 chains. He’s the founder of TRON, CEO of BitTorrent and owner of two crypto exchanges.

Our research team ranked him second only to Satoshi Nakamoto in September. https://t.co/EvSkbZ5vLT

— Arkham (@arkham) October 12, 2026

The figures are of assets that Arkham reports holding on Sun, and not a public statement of his total net worth. The market price and transfers transmit the balance of the circulation of wallets as well.

In its black-and-white depiction, Sun is said to be TRON’s founder, BitTorrent’s CEO and the owner of two crypto exchanges. Additionally, the platform states that his research team had ranked him second only to Satoshi Nakamoto in September, but even this may not be an independently released wealth ranking.

Read More: Justin Sun Files $45M Lawsuit Over Frozen WLFI Tokens in Trump-Linked Clash

SUSDS and STETH Dominate Sun’s Portfolio

The dashboard shows a high asset concentration in the limited number of assets. SUSDS makes up the biggest spot, followed by STETH and Bitcoin.

According to Arkham, SUSDS currently holds Sun’s biggest stake of 986.337 million tokens valued at $1.09 billion. His portfolio also includes 238,861 STETH valued at $607.55 million, 4,042 BTC worth $336.73 million, and 1,690 WBTC valued at $140.64 million. Other smaller investments are the 544.719 million WLFI at $31.03 million, the 39.226 million STRX with a value of $17.34 million, and the 6.875 million TRX valued at about $2.28 million.

Read More: FDUSD in the Crosshairs: Justin Sun’s $500M Fraud Accusation and First Digital’s Rebuttal

Stablecoin Exposure Stands Out

This is because SUSDS represents almost half of the monitored portfolio and is the most important position on the dashboard. The token is linked to Sky’s savings stablecoin platform and STETH is a staked Ether asset exposure.

The holdings prove that Sun is not just holding the native token, TRX, of the TRON network. But the balance of wallets says nothing about whether positions are held for investment, how many are used in treasury or are used for collateral purposes.

On-Chain Data Offers a Window into Crypto Wealth

Blockchain explorers allow researchers to monitor public addresses, token balances, and transfers across supported networks. Arkham’s labels aid in the connection of addresses that have been known to the same entity without focusing just on individual wallets.

Nevertheless, there are some restrictions to address attribution. Assets can exist in hides, custodians or organizations with complicated ownership structures and not all wallets are identifiable with an individual.

Arkham’s latest snapshot therefore offers a detailed look at the crypto assets it associates with Sun, while leaving his complete financial position beyond the reach of on-chain balances alone.

title: Ledger Investigates Fund Losses Tied to Southeast Asian Reseller After Implant Found in Device
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Ledger Investigates Fund Losses Tied to Southeast Asian Reseller After Implant Found in Device
Ledger has reassured users after people who bought signing devices from a Malaysia-based reseller reported losing funds.  
This post Ledger Investigates Fund Losses Tied to Southeast Asia...
content:
Ledger has said it is working with authorities after users last week reported losing funds and one received a tampered device. But the company reassured customers that the number of impacted products was “limited.” 

The hardware wallet manufacturer added in an announcement on Sunday that it had reached out to affected customers. 

Paris-based Ledger on Friday said it had started an investigation after customers in South East Asia reported they’d lost funds after buying from a reseller. 

Then, on Saturday, Ledger said it confirmed that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. 

Ledger would not confirm the amount of money lost but blockchain investigator Specter said $86 million had been drained from devices. 

“As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities,” Ledger wrote on Sunday. 

It added: “Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.

“Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes.”

Customers in South East Asia last week reported losing funds after buying from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia-based vendor CryptoBilis. 

Ledger then advised customers who’d bought from CryptoBilis to not set up their devices. 

CryptoBilis has since stopped selling its hardware wallets, Ledger said on Sunday. 

People on social media posted picture evidence of devices implanted into Ledger products, claiming it could get users’ private keys. It isn’t clear how many of Ledger’s signing devices contained the implant. 

Neither Ledger nor CryptoBilis immediately responded to questions from Bitcoin Magazine. 

Hardware wallet security has been a hot topic ever since hackers in July were able to steal close to $120 million in bitcoin from Coldcard users. 

The products, made by Canadian company Coinkite, contained a firmware bug which led to faulty seed generation, allowing hackers to essentially guess investor seedphrases. 

In a separate incident, hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor last month reported that close to 81,000 customers had their details leaked after its third-party fulfillment partner had data stolen. 

Criminals have been targeting data this year, with scammers getting hold of customer information via crypto wallet Ledger’s payment processor Global-e to send phishing emails. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

Geneva, Switzerland, October 12, 2026 — TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), today highlighted key findings from its State of TRON Q3 2026 ecosystem report. The report examines network activity, stablecoin settlement, liquidity, tokenomics, developer activity, decentralization, and protocol governance during the third quarter of 2026.

TRON surpassed $30 trillion in cumulative transaction volume in Q3 2026, marking another milestone for a network used as infrastructure for stablecoin settlement and digital-asset transfers. At the same time, stablecoin supply and total value locked continued to expand, while the network’s active-address base grew and transaction activity remained broadly steady.

Key Insights

  • In Q3, TRON surpassed $30 trillion in cumulative transaction volume. Stablecoin settlement reached $2.21 trillion in the Q3 reporting period, with average daily volume rising 3.9% from Q2 to $24.05 billion.
  • Canary Capital launched the Canary Staked TRX ETF (TRXS) on September 9, 2026. TRXS gives investors exposure to the spot price of TRX—the native utility and governance token of the TRON blockchain network—alongside passive net staking rewards reflected directly in the fund’s daily net asset value. TRON DAO’s team rang the Cboe Closing Bell in Chicago on September 29 to celebrate its launch.
  • TRON expanded its ecosystem collaborations in Q3 2026, adding institutional custody and staking, new trading venues, and digital dollar products through Anchorage Digital, Bitnomial, Backpack, Ethena, and Ducat. Payment, wallet, cross-chain, and developer integrations also broadened access and strengthened the infrastructure for payment, treasury, and DeFi applications. 
  • Stablecoin supply and Total Value Locked continued to expand. USDT and USDD supply reached $93.88 billion, up 5.5% from Q2, while TVL including staking hit $28.21 billion and TVL excluding staking (DeFi TVL) hit $13.05 billion
  • The active-address base widened while transaction frequency held steady. Average rolling monthly active addresses increased 9.8% to 18 million. 
  • Network fee generation moderated. Fees totaled $701.4 million during Q3, averaging $7.62 million per day, down 4.0% from Q2. The average daily transaction fee fell from $0.668 to $0.643. 

TRON’s ecosystem continued to broaden in Q3, with new integrations spanning institutional services, trading, stablecoins, payments, wallets, and developer infrastructure. Anchorage Digital added TRX staking and TRC-20 custody, while Bitnomial and Backpack expanded access to TRX markets. Ethena brought USDe and sUSDe to TRON, and Ducat connected its Bitcoin-backed financial infrastructure to the network’s stablecoin ecosystem.

The quarter also brought new capabilities for users and developers. MoonPay introduced gasless transactions through Trust Wallet, removing the need to hold TRX for network fees, while Bitcoin.com Wallet added native support for TRX and USDT-TRC20. MetaMask connectivity expanded across B.AI, SUN.io, JustLend DAO, and BitTorrent, while Fireblocks Flow added support for payments from TRON wallets. Eco and STON.fi expanded cross-chain stablecoin connectivity, and KiiChain linked TRON assets with its 24/7 foreign-exchange and payment infrastructure. For developers, Privy expanded wallet, transaction, and policy-management capabilities, while OpenZeppelin brought its smart contract libraries and security tooling to the network. Together, these integrations strengthened the infrastructure available for payments, treasury management, and DeFi applications on TRON.

TRON’s third-quarter developments underscore continued growth in stablecoin settlement, liquidity, network activity, and ecosystem infrastructure, reflecting sustained demand for its financial infrastructure. With these trends strengthening, TRON enters Q4 with an increasingly established role in global stablecoin settlement and digital asset activity.

Read the full report from TRON here.

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of October 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 408 million in total user accounts, more than 15 billion in total transactions, and over $28 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”
