title: Trade Republic Profit Jumps Sevenfold in Final Full Year with German PFOF
summary:
Trade Republic's annual profit rose almost sevenfold to €232.7 million as commission income more than doubled. The figures provide the final full-year benchmark before Germany’s payment-for-order-flow exemption expired. 
According to Trade Republic’s newly filed financial statements for the year end...
content:
2026-10-12T19:05:00.000+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 17:05 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Trade Republic’s profit jumped to €232.7 million in the final full financial year before Germany’s PFOF exemption expired.
  • Commission income rose 132% to €732.6 million, while a slower increase in costs reduced the cost-to-income ratio from 83% to 62%.

Trade Republic's annual profit rose almost sevenfold to €232.7 million as commission income more than doubled. The figures provide the final full-year benchmark before Germany’s payment-for-order-flow exemption expired.

According to Trade Republic’s newly filed financial statements for the year ended September 2025, commission income rose because of higher trading volumes and a broader product range. Costs also rose, but much more slowly than revenue, driving a sharp improvement in profitability.

Profit Reaches €232.7 Million

Commission income rose 132% to €732.6 million, while interest income declined slightly as lower rates offset growth in interest-bearing cash reserves and bank balances.

Operating costs also increased, but more slowly than income. Administrative expenses rose 87% to €419.8 million, including higher spending on marketing, technology and outsourced services. Consequently, the cost-to-income ratio improved to 62% from 83%.

Financial measure2024/252023/24Change
Net profit€232.7m€34.8m+569%
Commission income€732.6m€315.6m+132%
Interest income€21.0m€23.0m-8%
Administrative expenses€419.8m€224.6m+87%
Equity€799.3m€566.5m+41%

The results preceded a €1.2 billion secondary share transaction that valued Trade Republic at €12.5 billion. The transaction involved existing shares and did not provide new capital to the company, which reported more than 10 million customers and €150 billion in client assets.

The Commission Engine Behind the Profit

Trade Republic’s non-financial report describes the execution model operating during the period: all trades were conducted through LS Exchange, while customers generally paid a fixed €1 third-party-cost fee. Savings-plan executions were free.

The financial statements show that commission income covered execution-related subsidies, customer fees, payment services and other commission items. Those subsidies included rebates received for routing securities orders to trading partners.

PFOF rebates formed part of Trade Republic’s commission income during the period, but the financial statements do not disclose their value. It is therefore impossible to determine how much of the increase from €315.6 million to €732.6 million came from routing payments.

Trade Republic attributed the wider increase to higher trading volumes, an expanded product range and continued international growth.

The Post-PFOF Test Begins

After Germany’s PFOF exemption expired on 30 June 2026, Trade Republic introduced two execution options.

Under the standard Best Price model, the company selects the execution venue based on prices available across the relevant exchanges and charges €1 per order.

Clients who want to choose the venue themselves can use Direct Price. This option provides access to 30 exchanges and costs €2 per order. Finance Magnates previously examined the new structure.

Despite the approaching ban, management said in the report that it expected another significant absolute increase in commission income during the following financial year and had adapted its strategy accordingly.

Separately, Trade Republic Business III GmbH received approval to operate a multilateral trading facility on 23 January 2026. The accounts do not explain its intended role or connect it to the new execution model.

The next accounts will provide the first evidence of how the new model performs, although only the final three months of that financial year fall after the German PFOF exemption expired.

title: Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals
summary: The Bitcoin mining industry needs roughly $50 billion to complete planned AI infrastructure projects, with IREN, Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital facing major funding gaps.
content:
Bitcoin mining companies expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing face sharply different borrowing costs as lenders scrutinize large-scale data center projects, adding to the industry’s growing financing challenges.

According to the latest Miner Weekly newsletter from BlocksBridge Consulting, securing major AI customers has only been part of the challenge for miners. Companies must also raise billions of dollars to purchase computing equipment, build facilities and secure the power infrastructure needed to fulfill their contracts.

“[B]ig lenders have become more selective about data center loans and decisions increasingly depend on the customer, the contract and the path to completion,” BlocksBridge said.

IREN, which has expanded from Bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure, illustrates the differences in financing costs. The company secured a $3.65 billion GPU financing package in June at a blended interest rate of 6%, followed by a separate $2.4 billion financing arrangement in August at a fixed rate of 9%. The two agreements cover different projects, so they’re not directly comparable, but they show how borrowing costs can vary even within the same company.

Financing arrangements can also carry costs beyond interest payments. In a separate transaction involving Cipher Digital, Google agreed to backstop $1.4 billion in lease obligations in exchange for warrants representing 5.4% of Cipher’s equity, subject to certain adjustments. Exercising those warrants could dilute existing shareholders.

The financing requirements highlight a broader challenge for Bitcoin miners entering the AI market. Even companies with multibillion-dollar customer contracts may need substantial additional capital before their data centers become operational.

Related: Hut 8, IREN deals lift AI-focused Bitcoin mining stocks

Bitcoin miners face massive AI funding gap

The differences in financing costs come as Bitcoin miners take on billions of dollars in debt to fund their AI expansion plans. At the height of the Bitcoin bull market last October, VanEck data showed that miners’ debt had surged roughly 500% from the second quarter of 2024.

Ironically, capital requirements have continued to grow during the Bitcoin bear market as miners shift away from BTC mining amid deteriorating economics. A June 2026 analysis by BlocksBridge Consulting, citing VanEck data, estimated that publicly traded Bitcoin miners needed roughly $50 billion to complete their planned AI infrastructure projects, including a $21.1 billion funding gap at IREN alone.

Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital also face substantial funding requirements, estimated at $7.2 billion and $4.6 billion, respectively.

Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

title: Palantir's Europe head warns the region is 'missing the boat' on AI just as it did with the internet
summary: The Palantir UK chief said the U.S. is racing ahead on enterprise AI while Europe hesitates, and explained why he thinks the company faces intense political attacks.
content:
Oct 12, 2026, 12:18 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Palantir’s head of U.K. and Europe Louis Mosley warned that Europe’s cautious approach to artificial intelligence risks repeating its failure to capitalize on the internet economy.
  • Mosley described Palantir as a proxy for AI adoption, citing strong growth in its U.S. commercial revenue while European companies remain hesitant.
  • Palantir faces European opposition over its defense and law enforcement contracts, but Mosley argued that political controversy distracts from AI’s potential to improve public services and productivity.

Palantir (PLTR) head of U.K. and Europe Louis Mosley warned that the region is making the same mistake with artificial intelligence (AI) that it made with the internet.

Where the U.S. "got the internet right," built a score of businesses and became the backbone of the digital economy, Europe "missed the boat," Mosley told CoinDesk in an interview.

The divergence between the markets in the decades since has been stark. Europe and the U.S. were roughly comparable 20 years ago on GDP per capita, capital-market depth and the scale of their largest companies. Since then, the U.S. has compounded growth while Europe has barely advanced in comparison.

Previous technology waves produced European champions. The internet wave produced almost none, with ASML (ASML) the rare exception, he said.

“It’s by far and away the largest European company. Which is, it tells you that the value is in tech,” he said.

Mosley, Palantir's executive vice president for the U.K and Europe, argued AI will be even more consequential. European corporates remain cautious, with an attitude of “This is new, that means it could be risky. I’ll wait and see,” according to Mosley.

Palantir builds an ontology and governance scaffold that lets governments and companies deploy large language models and agents in healthcare, industry or defense.

Mosley called the company “the purest proxy on public markets for the rate of AI adoption in an economy.” Palantir is model-agnostic: customers can run OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, open-weight models or Chinese systems and fine-tune them on their own data.

Opposition to Palantir across the U.K. and Europe stems from its deep defense and law enforcement ties, including providing surveillance software to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) under the administration of President Donald Trump and supplying targeting systems to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). Campaigners have argued against the use of Palantir in systems used by the public services such as the U.K.'s National Health Service (NHS) on ethical grounds.

“The issues that really get those people fired up are Gaza and Trump," Mosley told CoinDesk. "Palantir has contracts in America for Trump’s administration and has contracts in Israel with the IDF and we have a contract with the NHS.”

Mosley called this a distraction from domestic priorities, asking whether politicians would tell a constituent they must wait longer for a hip operation because of a supplier’s unrelated foreign contracts.

Political hostility to energy-intensive tech is commonplace: bitcoin miners were attacked over electricity use a decade ago. Many of them have now pivoted to AI high-performance computing and face identical criticism over power consumption.

While it’s true AI will disrupt jobs, it will also free nurses and police from paperwork, raising productivity, he said. With only around 1,000 customers against a far larger addressable market of complex organizations in allied countries, Mosley said he still sees Palantir as early.

The biggest risk to AI, he said, remains political failure to explain why the technology is good for people.

“You’re making all the same mistakes again,” Mosley noted of the recurring political response. “In the end, I want to believe that good wins out over bad.”

title: Strategy Smash Buys $21.5M in BTC as It Continues Bitcoin Accumulation
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy Smash Buys $21.5M in BTC as It Continues Bitcoin Accumulation
Bitcoin juggernaut Strategy has bought more BTC as it pivots back to accumulating on a weekly basis.  The Nasdaq-listed bitcoin treasury spent $21.5 million on 250 bitcoins from October 5 and October 11, accordi...
content:
Bitcoin juggernaut Strategy has bought more BTC as it pivots back to accumulating on a weekly basis. 

The Nasdaq-listed bitcoin treasury spent $21.5 million on 250 bitcoins from October 5 and October 11, according to a Monday filing. 

It added that it also spent $192.4 million repurchasing its STRC preferred stock. 

Strategy now holds 848,250 bitcoins worth $70.2 billion at today’s prices. Its stock (MSTR) on Monday was trading nearly 2% higher. 

The company — formerly MicroStrategy — has spent the past four weeks buying bitcoins after months of more sporadic buys or sometimes halting purchases for months altogether in order to build a bigger cash buffer. 

Monday’s filing also shows that the company bought last week’s bitcoin using net proceeds from MSTR Stock sales with its USD Cash buffer. Strategy has two cash reserves: “USD Reserve”, used to support the payment of dividends on the company’s preferred stock offerings and interest on its outstanding indebtedness, and “USD Cash”, which it uses to buy bitcoin. 

It first bought the cryptocurrency in 2020 to protect its shareholders from inflation. Since then, it has aggressively bought the asset and pivoted to being a bitcoin treasury. 

Investors can now buy its shares to get heightened exposure to the cryptocurrency, or get paid a yield via its digital credit products. 

The company is now focusing on products that pay investors yield via its STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD preferred shares. 

Its Nasdaq-listed stock is down over 50% over the past year after the price of bitcoin took a hit. 

But since the company started buying bitcoin in August 2020, MSTR has appreciated by nearly 1,000%. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: A7 to unveil a service that will re-invent the international payments market
summary: Moscow, Russia, 12th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Moscow, Russia, 12th October 2026, Chainwire

Moscow, Russia, October 12th, 2026, Chainwire

On 13 October, the Russian international settlement system A7, created by Bank PSB, is set to present A7 International, a service enabling payments for a foreign counterparty’s invoice in USDT, with the funds arriving via a standard SWIFT bank transfer in the required currency.

The service will cater primarily to foreign trade operators, but individuals are also eligible customers. The fee remains fixed at 0.3 percent.

Petr Fradkov, Chairman of PJSC Bank PSB, and Ilan Shor, CEO of A7, will provide a glimpse into its new offering on 13 October at 13:13.

To join the live broadcast and learn about the new project, follow the links:

https://a7.biz/live

About A7:

A7 is a global financial technology company specializing in international payments and settlement solutions for international trade. It was established in 2024 with the involvement of PSB Bank.

A7 is developing an independent global payment infrastructure across more than 100 countries, combining global financial expertise, advanced technology and regulatory compliance. The company’s products include international payments, digital financial assets and promissory notes.

A7 Group works with 15,000 clients, with around 2,000 transactions processed through the system every day. In 2025, approximately 19% of Russian companies’ cross-border trade settlements were processed through A7. In October 2025, A7 received an AA(RU) credit rating with a Stable outlook from ACRA.

content:
America is carrying $40 trillion in debt, and the dollar has lost about 30% of its purchasing power since 2020. Rep. Warren Davidson, founder of the Sound Money Caucus, explains why rising default risk and inflation are pushing rates higher, and why he believes people without real assets will lose purchasing power. He also warns that the future of Western civilization is centrally tied to the future of money.

title: FIS Launches AI Finance Suite; CFD Broker Accounts Show Cash Flow Swings
summary:

London's trading industry is coming home!
Cash flow...
content:
2026-10-12T17:05:00.000+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 15:05 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The platform combines internal and external data to support cash flow analysis and risk assessment.
  • Deloitte found 46% of finance leaders prioritised working capital optimisation for agentic AI.

FIS has launched an agentic AI suite for finance teams, including a module that forecasts cash flow across multiple time horizons. The FIS Agentic Insights Suite combines internal and external data to support cash flow analysis and risk assessment.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Cash flow management is also relevant to CFOs at retail CFD brokers, who oversee working capital, regulatory capital requirements and counterparty risks. Finance Magnates has reported that BP Prime's operator identified working capital needs and counterparty credit risk among its financial concerns.

One Global Market's latest accounts show that it generated £411K in operating cash flow in FY25, reversing a £710K outflow a year earlier. Changes in working capital accounted for much of the improvement.

AI Suite Combines Internal and External Data

The importance of working capital management is also reflected in Deloitte's Finance Trends 2026 survey. It found that 46% of global finance leaders identified working capital optimisation as a priority area for agentic AI, while 14% said they had fully integrated AI agents into their finance functions.

The platform combines data from enterprise resource planning, treasury and customer relationship management systems with external credit bureau and public data. FIS said this is designed to reduce manual data reconciliation across finance, credit and treasury teams.

FIS Adds Machine Learning to Cash Forecasting

The cash flow forecasting module uses machine learning and simulations to model different scenarios, including delayed incoming payments and faster cash outflows. The suite also provides real-time account scoring, recommendations and dashboards through Microsoft Power BI. Users can submit questions in natural language.

“Most finance teams can tell you what happened to their cash last quarter; very few can tell you what happens next month with confidence,” said Andrés Choussy, President of Capital Markets at FIS.

The suite connects with FIS's receivables products, GETPAID and BillerIQ, and treasury products, Integrity and Quantum. FIS said deployment can take weeks rather than months.

Planned future releases include payment anomaly detection and dispute forecasting. The suite is also designed to help finance teams manage days sales outstanding, a measure of how long a business takes to collect payments .

title: Tokenized catastrophe bonds target the disaster-insurance gap
summary: A planned Bermuda issuance would put legal ownership onchain and seek capital for disaster risks that remain costly to insure.
content:
Oct 12, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Natural disasters caused $220 billion in economic losses last year, but insurance covered only $107 billion, leaving households, businesses and governments to bear the rest.
  • The catastrophe-bond market reached $65.6 billion in June, as insurers increasingly transferred disaster risks to investors despite persistent coverage gaps, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.
  • Harneys and dropRWA plan to issue tokenized catastrophe bonds in early 2027, potentially widening investor access through smaller ownership units while remaining subject to securities, insurance and investor-protection rules.

Natural disasters caused $220 billion in economic losses last year. Insurance covered only $107 billion of that bill, according to Swiss Re, leaving households, businesses and governments to absorb the rest.

Capital has continued to flow into catastrophe bonds. Catastrophe bonds, or cat bonds, let insurers pass the financial risk of a hurricane, wildfire or earthquake to capital-market investors. The market had $65.6 billion outstanding in June and new issuance reached $11.3 billion in the second quarter, the largest quarterly total on record, according to Artemis’ recent cat bond report.

Yet large parts of the loss from floods, typhoons and wildfires remain uninsured. In the Asia-Pacific, 91% of disaster losses in 2023 were uninsured, according to the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It also said limited claims data and catastrophe models can make it harder for insurers and reinsurers to price coverage, particularly in high-risk areas.

Harneys, a Bermuda-based law firm specializing in global insurance, and tokenization platform dropRWA plan to issue tokenized cat bonds early next year, with each token representing legal ownership of the catastrophe bond.

The proposal builds on a conventional market that has historically been available largely to specialist funds and large institutions. Many catastrophe-bond offerings carry minimum investments of $250,000 or more. Harneys and droppRWA are considering a structure that could accommodate smaller beneficial interests, though it would still need to comply with securities, insurance and investor-protection rules.

Henry Tucker, chief executive of specialist insurance group Hearns, said a tokenized structure does not turn disaster coverage into a casual retail investment. The capital is fully committed to cover a defined insurance risk. “You’re not buying a right to get paid by somebody else who’s bet the other way at the casino,” he told CoinDesk in an interview.

Tucker pointed to flood cover and typhoon protection in Southeast Asia as risks that can be difficult to place with conventional reinsurers, particularly when claims data is limited or loss estimates are uncertain. A specialist underwriter could use a tokenized structure to raise capital for a single defined risk and set out the assumptions and the return offered to investors.

There is a real-world precedent for using catastrophe bonds to finance public disaster protection. The World Bank arranged $200 million of hurricane coverage for Jamaica in May, replacing an earlier transaction that paid out after Hurricane Melissa in 2025. Jamaica’s finance minister, Fayval Williams, called catastrophe bonds “an important piece ensuring capital market access” for the country’s resilience strategy.

Tokenization will not make a hurricane, flood or wildfire less expensive, Tucker said. Nor will it guarantee cheaper insurance for people in exposed areas, he added. The firms’ argument is that a token serving as the legal ownership record, combined with smaller ownership units, could bring more investors into a market built to absorb extreme losses.

title: Singapore Sets New AI Risk Rules for Finance. What They Mean for Brokers
summary:
The
Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has drawn a clearer regulatory line
around the use of artificial intelligence in financial services. On 7 October
2026, the regulator published its Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk
Management, establishing supervisory expectations for financial
ins...
content:
2026-10-12T16:00:00.000+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 14:00 GMT by Sylwester Majewski

  • MAS mandates phased compliance starting October 2027, requiring core risk governance within a year before full operational lifecycle controls hit in 2028.
  • Proportional expectations apply across all licensed entities, from banks to OTC brokers, increasing strictness based on application risk rather than flat prohibitions.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has drawn a clearer regulatory line around the use of artificial intelligence in financial services. On 7 October 2026, the regulator published its Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management, establishing supervisory expectations for financial institutions using AI, from traditional machine-learning models to Generative AI and increasingly autonomous AI agents. The guidelines follow a public consultation launched in November 2025 and will begin taking effect on 7 October 2027.

AI is increasingly moving beyond chatbots and productivity tools into areas that can influence financial decisions, customer interactions, compliance, risk management and potentially execution itself. MAS specifically warns that AI agents with access to tools could autonomously perform erroneous or unauthorised actions. It also identifies financial, operational, conduct, financial crime and reputational risks arising from AI, alongside security, privacy and third-party risks associated particularly with Generative AI.

A Framework Built Around Risk, Not a Ban on AI

The framework is not designed to slow the adoption of AI. Its central idea is proportionality. MAS expects financial institutions to understand where AI is being used, determine how important and risky each application is, and then apply controls that match that risk. A tool used to proofread an internal email clearly does not require the same controls as an AI model influencing investment recommendations or customer risk assessments.

London's trading industry is coming home!

This distinction is important when considering whether the framework is "mandatory". These are guidelines setting out MAS' supervisory expectations, rather than a standalone piece of legislation imposing identical technical requirements on every company. Yet regulated firms should not interpret this as optional guidance. MAS states that all financial institutions should adhere to its high-level expectations when deploying AI, while implementation should be proportionate to their size, activities and AI risk exposure. The guidelines also complement existing MAS requirements and principles, including Fairness, Ethics, Accountability and Transparency, known as FEAT.

MAS AI Guidelines: Implementation Timeline
DateRequirements
November 2025Public consultation launched
7 October 2026AI guidelines published
7 October 2027AI oversight, risk management and policies
7 October 2028AI lifecycle controls, capabilities and infrastructure

This gives firms roughly one year to establish the core governance layer and another year to complete the broader operational framework. MAS has also said that it intends to consult the industry in 2027 on whether further guidance specifically addressing agentic AI would be useful.

Who Needs to Follow the Guidelines?

The scope is broad. MAS says the guidelines apply to all financial institutions and all forms of AI technology. The categories listed by the regulator include banks, fund managers, financial advisers, insurers, payment institutions, exchanges, clearing houses, custodians, credit rating agencies and firms dealing in capital markets products. Exempt futures and OTC derivatives brokers are also explicitly included among the categories covered.

title: Cardano Price Prediction: Can ADA Break $0.32 and Target $0.70 as Whale Activity Surges?
summary: Cardano price holds near $0.25 as whale activity hits its highest level since June, with traders watching $0.32 for bullish breakout confirmation.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ADA

Cardano price holds near $0.25 as whale activity hits its highest level since June, with traders watching $0.32 for bullish breakout confirmation.

Cardano’s recovery is drawing fresh attention as whale activity reaches its highest level since June, but ADA still has a major hurdle to clear. Trading near $0.25, price needs to break above $0.31-$0.32 to strengthen the recovery and make a longer-term move towards $0.70 more credible. For now, buyers need to defend the $0.22-$0.25 base to keep that outlook intact.

Cardano Price Needs a Weekly Close Above $0.323

Cardano price is approaching an important weekly decision point after recovering from the $0.14-$0.15 region. ADA has pushed back into the same trend band that previously acted as resistance before the November 2024 breakout. Still, price has not yet established enough strength to confirm that another bullish transition is underway.

The weekly trend model shared by Trend Rider places $0.323 as the main confirmation level. A weekly close above this area would move ADA beyond the bearish trend band and signal that the larger structure is beginning to turn bullish. Until that happens, price remains vulnerable to rejection while trading inside the band.

The downside levels are equally clear. A close below about $0.22 would weaken the recovery and bring $0.18 back into focus, with the larger $0.14 support region next if selling pressure accelerates. This leaves ADA in a transitional phase, with $0.323 acting as the bullish trigger and $0.22 defining the first major risk level.

Cardano needs a weekly close above $0.323 to flip the broader trend bullish. Source: Trend Rider via X

Cardano Price Prediction Targeting $0.3136

Cardano’s weekly structure is improving after price pushed above the long-running descending trendline and reclaimed the bull market support band. That combination matters because ADA is no longer only bouncing from the $0.15 area; it is now trying to hold above the same trend structure that previously capped the recovery.

The chart shared by The Boss shows the bull market support band clustered around the low-$0.22 region, with ADA trading back above it near $0.255. The $0.2242 and $0.2268 area therefore becomes more than simple horizontal support. It now overlaps with the moving support band and the rising black trendline, creating a broader confluence zone that bulls need to keep intact.

Above current price, $0.3136 is the first major resistance and the next clear test of the recovery. A clean break through that level would open $0.3825, followed by $0.4488 if momentum continues.

ADA has broken trendline resistance and reclaimed the bull market support band. Source: The Boss via X

Cardano Whale Activity and Larger Wallet Holdings Build Around $0.25-$0.27

Cardano is seeing a clear increase in large-holder activity while ADA attempts to stabilize around the $0.25-$0.27 region. Santiment data shows 157 whale transactions worth more than $100,000, the highest level since June 4, while social dominance has climbed to 1.16%, its highest reading of 2026. That combination suggests that attention is rising at the same time bigger market participants are becoming more active.

Cardano whale transactions reach their highest level since June 4 as ADA social dominance hits a 2026 high of 1.16%. Source: Angry Crypto Show via X

The wallet distribution data shared by konnektr points in the same direction. Addresses holding more than 1 million ADA have continued increasing their total holdings even as the number of wallets in that category trends lower, indicating that more supply is becoming concentrated among fewer large holders.

Cardano supply data. Source: konnektr via X

Smaller wallets are showing the opposite pattern. The number of addresses holding less than 100 ADA has been increasing, but their combined holdings continue to decline. That creates a noticeable divergence between growing participation at the lower end and stronger concentration among the largest balances.

If this trend continues while ADA holds the $0.25-$0.27 region, it would provide a supportive on-chain backdrop ahead of the next technical test. The market still needs to clear $0.31-$0.32 for stronger confirmation, but rising whale activity and larger-holder concentration suggest that interest is building before that breakout attempt.

October Overall Crypto Momentum

October has opened with noticeably higher volatility across Bitcoin and Ethereum, but neither market has established a clean directional move yet. That uncertainty is keeping pressure on the wider altcoin market, where breakouts are becoming more dependent on whether BTC can settle into a stronger trend rather than continuing to swing inside a volatile range.

For Cardano, the timing is important because ADA is already approaching the $0.31-$0.32 resistance zone. If Bitcoin begins to recover with stronger follow-through and Ethereum also stabilizes, Cardano would have a better chance to extend its own breakout attempt.

Until then, ADA may continue to struggle for sustained acceptance above resistance, with broader crypto momentum likely to remain one of the main factors shaping the next move.

Cardano Price Analysis: $0.70 Could Shape the Route Toward $1.90

Cardano’s longer-term setup is beginning to resemble an earlier cycle structure, although the comparison does not imply that the same percentage move will repeat. Jesse Peralta highlights the current recovery from the $0.20-$0.25 region alongside ADA’s 2020 base, where a strong initial advance was followed by a deep retracement before the larger trend accelerated.

The scenario places $0.70 as the first major upside level if ADA can continue building above its present range. From there, a pullback toward roughly $0.55 would still fit the historical structure rather than automatically invalidate it, provided buyers continue defending the broader recovery.

A successful hold above that retracement zone would then place greater emphasis on $1.90 as the next larger target in the sequence. The chart therefore frames the move less as a straight rally and more as a possible progression of expansion, correction and renewed continuation.

For now, the nearer technical levels remain important. ADA still needs to establish itself above the $0.31-$0.32 resistance area before the $0.70 objective becomes more credible.

Cardano’s historical cycle comparison outlines a potential move towards $0.70, followed by $1.90. Source: Jesse Peralta via X

What Traders Should Watch Next

Cardano’s next move is likely to depend on whether the $0.22-$0.25 base continues to hold while price works through the $0.31-$0.32 resistance zone. The recovery has gained support from stronger whale activity and improving wallet concentration, but those signals still need confirmation from price before the broader trend can be considered decisively stronger.

A sustained break above $0.31-$0.32 would improve the case for a move toward $0.38 and higher, while another rejection could keep ADA confined to its current range.

Broader crypto momentum will also remain important, particularly if Bitcoin and Ethereum begin to establish a clearer direction after a volatile start to October.

title: Silver Price Analysis: XAG/USD Risks Dropping Toward $54.76
summary: The big drop in silver prices from $95 indicates a sharp reversal from an explosive move that had been in progress.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

The big drop in silver prices from $95 indicates a sharp reversal from an explosive move that had been in progress.

The metal’s bull market has been curtailed by the pullback, and a longer time frame money flow indicator is negative.

One analyst now believes that silver will see the lower weekly BB at $54.76 by November. But if the recovery breaches the 20-week moving average, then the bearish perspective would be wiped out.

Silver Price Faces Lower Bollinger Band Test by November

After a sharp rise in 2026, the silver price is off to a fresh phase in its bear market run. The silver price is back on the downside after bouncing off the highs it reached in 2026. Silver analyst CyclesFan predicted that silver might break its lower weekly BB by November in a recent X post.

The analyst says the bottom of the indicator is at $54.76 right now. Silver is losing steam from its highs and trading around 60-65 on the weekly chart.

The chart’s middle Bollinger Band, which tracks the 20-week moving average, provides another level to watch. Source: CyclesFa Via X

A weekly closing price above that average would call into question the short-term bearish forecast, said the analyst.

Against the backdrop of Silver’s recent price action, the cautious assessment is justifiable. While the metal rallied significantly in early 2026, it turned around and started getting lower highs. Recoveries since then have not regained the momentum that had been gained upwards.

The lower Bollinger Band line then may serve as a downward price objective if the trend of selling persists. Transitions between approximately $60.82 and $54.76 would be about 10%.

The indicator does not, however, give a guaranteed price target but rather a potential price reference. If this occurs and prices fall below the band again, but buyers return, silver could stabilize before hitting the band.

Silver Price Chart Shows Retreat From 2026 Peak

Separately, The Technical chart from TradingView is a longer timeframe view of silver compared to the USD (XAG/USD). The price displayed is $60.82, which is 0.74% higher as of the October 10, 2026, data.

This chart shows the price of silver from 2010 to 2026 in the month of October. The prices had been trading at significantly lower levels for several years before gradually rising in 2024 and 2025. Source: TradingView

The rally spurred up significantly at the end of 2025 and into early 2026. Indeed, silver had jumped into the vicinity of $95 and had staged a steep price move that was more pronounced than its longer trading history.

It was followed by a large correction. The stock has fallen from its highs and is now selling significantly lower than its earlier this-year highs.

That decline has not been overcome with the latest recovery. Silver has rallied off its recent lows, but the chart shows the metal is struggling to regain its upward trend.

Silver Price Momentum Weakens as Money Flow Turns Negative

Meanwhile, Silver continues to trade above several historical price levels, but the rapid turnaround has dampened the immediate bull market.

The momentum of silver has weakened with a fall in the Money Flow Indicator this week. The money flow indicator turned negative this week, making silver price momentum wane.

The TradingView chart also features the Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) indicator, which illustrates buying and selling energy based on price and quantity. It has just moved down from the neutral zero line with its last reading of -0.08.

If the reading is negative, it indicates that the selling pressure has surpassed the buying pressure within the indicator’s time frame. This comes on the heels of the cautionary note from silver’s pullback from its 2026 highs.

The chart also indicates that there was a lot of trading activity around the steep rise and subsequent pullback. This trend suggests that the recent timeframe has witnessed significant market participation and increased price fluctuations.

The $54.76 lower Bollinger Band is the key reference line to watch for from a technical perspective in the X post. But silver must continue its recent recovery and break back above the 20-week moving average to head back toward the bull case.

The TradingView chart is not creating its own clear support level at $54.76. This is according to another weekly Bollinger Band study shared by CyclesFan.

Traders will be alert for the possibility that buyers step in to support silver if it nears the bottom of the lower band or for more price action to break down the bottom. A continuation of prices above the 20-week moving average would, on the other hand, question the analyst’s bearish bias.

The two charts thus suggest a market strengthening from a significant correction, while the momentum indicators remain bearish.

ZFX has been named winner of the ‘Best Trading Conditions’ award at the UF AWARDS APAC 2026, presented during iFX EXPO Asia 2026. The award confirms what ZFX has worked toward for years: transparent, secure and technology-driven trading.

Part of Zeal Group, a portfolio of regulated financial institutions and fintech companies specialising in multi-asset liquidity, ZFX serves both retail and institutional investors across forex, commodities, indices, stocks and cryptocurrencies via CFDs. Founded in 2017 by a group of experienced traders, the company has grown into a multi-asset brokerage with a widening footprint across Greater China, Southeast Asia, Latin America, South Africa, India and Dubai. For a broker of that reach, trading conditions are not a single feature but the sum of pricing, execution, liquidity and the safeguards behind every position.

What the award recognises

At its core, Best Trading Conditions is a recognition of cost and execution quality. Behind this sits the company's institutional-grade liquidity. ZFX has established a highly diversified liquidity pool and prime brokerage relationships, allowing it to operate as a competitive matched principal broker and source pricing directly from the institutional marketplace. Paired with millisecond-level execution, it keeps spreads tight even when markets move fast.

A market-neutral model built on transparency

ZFX's competitive pricing is built on its institutional-grade liquidity. The company has established a highly diversified liquidity pool and prime brokerage relationships, allowing it to operate as a competitive matched principal broker and source pricing directly from the institutional marketplace. Paired with millisecond-level execution, it keeps spreads tight even when markets move fast.

Regulation and the security of client funds

"Winning this award validates our ongoing efforts to create a secure, fair, and transparent trading environment. At ZFX, our core mission has always been to build unwavering trust with our clients and to elevate their trading experience through cutting-edge technology continuously," said the CEO of ZFX.

A growing presence across Asia-Pacific

The award also reflects ZFX's growing influence across the Asia-Pacific trading community, supported by an active engagement programme through 2025 and 2026. In May 2026, the company hosted a premium client and partner experience day at Sha Tin Racecourse in Hong Kong, pairing a tour of its Hong Kong office with client networking.

The recognition reflects the standard ZFX holds across every market it serves: regulated operations, competitive liquidity, dependable technology and client-focused trading conditions.

title: What AI Actually Took From Bitcoin
summary:

content:
2026-10-12T14:09:34.579+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 12:09 GMT by Petr Sergeev

Disclaimer

  • Bitcoin recovered while the AI trade was still booming. That makes the old story about investors choosing one technological future over another much harder to argue.

Bitcoin needs to stop competing with AI for attention. If the case for owning it still depends on being the most exciting bet on the future, then years of institutionalisation have done less than crypto likes to admit.

For years, that asset had a very convenient advantage. It gave investors tech, finance, rebellion and the thrill of being early, all in a single liquid investment. AI now offers much of that excitement in a form traditional investors already know how to read through earnings, capital spending and companies with businesses they can actually model.

Crypto seems strangely worried by that. I am not. Bitcoin losing its monopoly on speculative excitement is only a problem if excitement was doing more of the work than the industry wants to acknowledge.

Back in June, there was an almost suspiciously convenient explanation for Bitcoin’s bad year - investors had simply found something more exciting. It was trading around $63,000, down almost a third in 2026, while semiconductor stocks were among the market’s biggest winners. Major semiconductor ETFs had taken in more than $21 billion that year, while Bitcoin ETFs had recorded roughly $3.1 billion in net outflows. Reuters described it as investors cooling on Bitcoin while chasing AI and a new wave of major tech listings. It was an easy story to believe. Maybe too easy.

By August, that explanation looked much less convincing. Bitcoin had climbed back above $80,000 and at one point was up 28% for the month, its strongest monthly gain since November 2024. AI enthusiasm had barely cooled. Nvidia jumped 8.7% after another strong forecast, while estimates for 2026 capital spending by Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle had risen from about $485 billion in January to roughly $730 billion by July.

Bitcoin was recovering while investors were still extremely enthusiastic about AI. I think crypto has been far too quick to confuse losing the spotlight with losing the investment case.

Bitcoin used to combine several ideas into one trade

If what you want is a clean play on technological acceleration, AI is hard to beat right now. The money is there, in corporate spending, in the race to build data centers and in the prices investors are willing to pay for the companies supplying the computing power.

This is where I think the June interpretation lost its way. The money leaving Bitcoin ETFs for semiconductor funds was real, but the conclusion was much harder to support. The asset had supposedly lost the “future trade,” and therefore part of its reason to exist. I do not buy that. That argument only works if it still needs technological novelty to attract capital, and I think that stopped being true years ago.

What AI seems to have taken from Bitcoin is not its ability to attract capital, but a role it once had almost to itself: the liquid bet that let investors feel they had spotted the future before everyone else. But its ownership base looks very different now. Regulated products have opened it to funds that once would not have touched it, while investors with no interest in crypto culture are perfectly comfortable discussing Bitcoin as a monetary asset.

It can still be speculative, volatile and deeply irrational at times. But plenty of people buying it today are not trying to discover the next technology before everyone else. AI did not take those reasons away. It took over one job Bitcoin used to perform exceptionally well: making investors feel that they had spotted the future early.

I think crypto gives up far too much by treating the loss of that job as a loss for Bitcoin itself. But that is only half of the argument. In the second part, I want to look at why crypto is so uncomfortable with losing that role, and whether Bitcoin actually needs it back.

title: Standard Chartered offers RLUSD custody in Dubai and plans LMAX collateral link
summary: Ripple previously gave LMAX $150 million in financing to integrate RLUSD into its institutional infrastructure.
content:
Oct 12, 2026, 8:09 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Standard Chartered’s Dubai branch now offers regulated institutional custody of Ripple’s dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.
  • The bank and LMAX Group plan to let clients use RLUSD held at Standard Chartered as trading collateral without transferring it to the venue, subject to testing, regulatory requirements and approvals.
  • The arrangement advances Ripple’s effort to establish RLUSD as an institutional settlement and collateral asset while expanding Standard Chartered’s digital-asset custody business.

Global bank giant Standard Chartered now offers institutional custody of Ripple’s USD-pegged stablecoin RLUSD on the XRP Ledger through its Dubai branch, giving eligible clients a regulated bank to hold the dollar-pegged stablecoin.

The bank, with nearly $450 billion in assets under management, also plans to work with Ripple and LMAX Group, an institutional trading venue for foreign exchange and digital assets, so clients can use RLUSD held at Standard Chartered as collateral for trading on LMAX’s platform. That part of the arrangement is not yet live and remains subject to documentation, testing, regulatory requirements and internal approvals, the bank said on Monday via email.

LMAX plans to allow clients to use RLUSD held at Standard Chartered to back trades, so they would not need to transfer the stablecoin to the venue.

That could appeal to banks, funds and other institutions that want to trade with stablecoins but do not want to leave the assets at a trading venue. It separates custody from execution: the bank holds the tokens and the venue accepts their value as collateral.

“Regulated custody connected to a global systemically important bank is becoming one of the most valuable pieces of infrastructure in digital assets,” said Joseph Goh, head of Asia-Pacific at Singapore-based crypto investment bank Areta.

Waqar Chaudry, Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets, securities services and transaction services, said “institutional clients want to participate in digital asset markets without compromising on how their assets are safeguarded or how risk is managed.”

The move builds on Ripple’s effort to position RLUSD as a settlement and collateral asset for institutions. Ripple provided LMAX with $150 million in financing in January as part of plans to embed the stablecoin in the group’s infrastructure, including for institutional trading.

The LMAX link, if completed, would give RLUSD another route into the collateral systems that sit behind institutional trading, rather than limiting the token to payments or spot settlement.

Standard Chartered has been expanding its custody operations in several financial centers. Last week, it said it planned to offer institutional clients in Singapore custody for selected cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets, having fully acquired Zodia Custody earlier this year It became the first bank to distribute one of Hong Kong’s two regulated stablecoins in August.

title: Ledger claims CryptoBilis cases are limited as up to $93 million is traced, $10 million frozen
summary: Ledger said every confirmed case involves devices sold by the Southeast Asian reseller, but critics say the hardware-wallet maker must answer for an authorized sales channel.
content:
Updated Oct 12, 2026, 9:42 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 12, 2026, 8:01 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Blockchain analytics firms estimate that attackers stole as much as $94.5 million from hundreds of wallets linked to Ledger devices sold by authorized reseller CryptoBilis, though Ledger has not confirmed the total.
  • Ledger found an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one affected device, while Tether froze $10 million in USDT tied to the theft and investigators continued tracing the funds.
  • Ledger advised CryptoBilis customers not to set up unused devices and urged those already using one to transfer their assets to a new device with a newly generated recovery phrase.

As much as $93.2 million in crypto was siphoned from wallets linked to the Ledger devices sold by the reseller CryptoBilis, according to several blockchain analytical and intelligence firms.

Tether has frozen $10 million in USDT tied to the theft, while Ledger said Sunday that the investigations into the theft, first reported three days ago, are still underway.

Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one affected device. The company did not say whether the stolen wallet was compromised in the same way or how the devices were tampered with.

Blockchain analysis and intelligence company Bitquery said it traced $93.2 million linked to the Ledger exploit. It said the hackers stole mostly USDT and TRON tokens from 315 wallets across six blockchains. Security research platform YFarmX reported a higher number, saying the attackers siphoned off $94.5 million from 521 addresses across seven blockchains. Both estimates are based on public blockchain data, not a confirmed Ledger loss total.

Ledger did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for confirmation of the amount stolen and whether it is considering a reimbursement plan for those affected by the exploit.

The Tether freeze, confirmed by Bitquery, is important because stablecoin issuers can block tokens linked to crime, unlike bitcoin or ether. Bitquery also said roughly $81 million could still be traced onchain as of Oct. 11, while some funds had moved through Tornado Cash and Zcash.

Tether did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment on the freeze.

Ledger’s effort to characterize the incident as confined to CryptoBilis has drawn pushback because the reseller was listed as authorized on Ledger’s website. “It’s not a CryptoBilis incident, it’s a Ledger incident,” X user MyCryptoParadise wrote. “At least take ownership of this mess.”

The episode is distinct from an April phishing campaign involving a fake Ledger Live app on Apple’s App Store, which drained at least $9.5 million after users entered their recovery phrases. This time, the attacker appears to have obtained the keys needed to directly empty hundreds of wallets.

Ledger advised CryptoBilis customers not to set up unused devices. Those who have already used one should move assets to a new device with a newly generated recovery phrase, it said.

title: Bitcoin falls below $83,000 as dollar strength keeps markets on edge
summary: Bitcoin and gold hold steady as a firm dollar and rising bond yields weigh on sentiment, while IREN secures a multiyear cloud services deal with Anthropic.
content:
coverage endedOct 12, 2026, 1:08 p.m. EDT

Bitcoin falls below $83,000 as dollar strength keeps markets on edge

Bitcoin and gold hold steady as a firm dollar and rising bond yields weigh on sentiment, while IREN secures a multiyear cloud services deal with Anthropic.

Nasdaq closes 0.7% lower as crypto stocks, BTC end Monday in the red

It was a day to forget for risk assets on Monday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 closing 0.7% lower amid weak U.S. trading.

Oil prices eased a bit in the later afternoon hours to near $93 a barrel, but still firmly higher during the day as supply concerns still linger.

Bitcoin BTC$82,292.69 clawed back some ground from its session lows, changing hands near $82,700 recently.

Crypto-related stocks also nursed losses, with Securitize extending its decline to 14%.

Miners, whose fortunes are now tied as much to the AI infrastructure and data center buildout as to bitcoin mining, were broadly lower. Bitdeer (BTDR), Cipher Mining CIFR$13.01·Market Closed, TeraWulf WULF$13.36·Market Closed and HIVE Digital HIVE$2.4050·Market Closed all nursed losses of roughly 3% to 4%.

Tokenization firm Securitize extended losses to 14%

Bitcoin, ether slides to session lows in weak afternoon trading

Bitcoin BTC$82,292.69 has slipped further during the U.S. trading session, hitting a session low of near $82,300 in a weak afternoon trading for risk assets.

Ether ETH$2,550.35 has now given back all its overnight gains, holding above $2,500 level by a thread.

The two largest cryptocurrencies lost 1.6% and 1.3%, respectively, over the past 24 hours. Other crypto majors including XRP, Solana (SOL) and Hyperliquid’s HYPE were also down 3%-4% during the same period.

Securitize slides 10% as crypto stocks lose ground in holiday trading

A mid-day check on the U.S. stock market shows most crypto-related stocks nursing losses, with tokenization firm Securitize (SECZ) leading the selling.

The firm’s shares fell more than 10% by midday, giving up most of the recent bounce fueled influential investment research firm Citrini's report featuring the company as one of the biggest beneficiary of Wall Street bringing equities onto blockchain rails.

Elsewhere, digital custodian BitGo BTGO$7.1530·Market Closed and institutional-focused exchange Bullish BLSH$31.64·Market Closed both slipped about 3%. USDC issuer Circle CRCL$83.87·Market Closed, bitcoin holder Strategy MSTR$152.73·Market Closed and ether treasury Bitmine BMNR$23.84·Market Closed nursed modest declines. Coinbase COIN$180.40·Market Closed held up with a 0.5% gain.

The weakness came as broader U.S. stocks struggled for direction. The S&P 500 was flat, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 0.5%.

Trading is taking place against a holiday backdrop, with the U.S. bond market and Canadian stock exchanges closed for the day. U.S. stock markets remain open.

Micron Technology breaks below $1,000

Micron Technology (MU) shares are down 4%, dropping below $1,000 for the first time since mid-September, as pressure spread beyond crypto to AI-related stocks. SanDisk (SNDK), which makes flash memory and storage products also declined 6%.

Bitcoin miners that have expanded into AI infrastructure also continued to surrender gains from earlier this year, with Cipher Digital CIFR$13.01·Market Closed, Bitdeer (BTDR) and HIVE Digital Technologies HIVE$2.4050·Market Closed each down around 3%.

Bitmine bought another $32 million in ETH

Bitmine buys another $32 million in ETH, now just weeks away from ending its buying spree

Bitmine BMNR$23.84·Market Closed bought another 12,532 ether ETH$2,550.35 over the past week, worth roughly $32 million at Monday's price of $2,536, bringing the company another step closer to ending its year-long buying spree.

That was the firm’s smallest weekly purchase since mid-August, as chairman Tom Lee last week said the company will stop buying ETH after reaching its goal to hold 5% of ether’s supply.

The latest purchase lifted Bitmine's holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, worth about $15.3 billion at current prices and representing roughly 4.9% of the cryptocurrency's total supply.

Strategy (MSTR) acquires 250 bitcoin for $21.5 million last week

Strategy MSTR$152.73·Market Closed acquired 250 bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, while spending $192.4 million repurchasing its variable-rate preferred stock, STRC.

The bitcoin purchases, made between Oct. 5 and Oct. 11 at an average price of $86,194 per coin, brought its total holdings to 848,250 BTC. Strategy has spent approximately $64 billion at an average cost of $75,444 per bitcoin.

The company funded the purchases with $21 million in net proceeds from selling 125,183 MSTR shares through its at-the-market (ATM) offering program, alongside $500,000 from its cash balance.

Strategy also repurchased approximately 1.93 million STRC shares, leaving $354.8 million available under its preferred stock repurchase program.

MSTR shares are up 1% pre-market

Markets start the week cautiously as U.S. dollar and bond yields stay firm

Markets are making a cautious start to the week, with bitcoin trading just above $83,000 and gold around $4,180 an ounce, both down roughly -0.5%. Tech futures are slightly lower, while WTI crude is edging higher above $92 a barrel. Bond yields are also ticking up as bond prices fall, following a brief recovery in the second half of last week that saw TLT, the long-dated U.S. Treasury ETF, gain more than 2%. The dollar remains firm, with the DXY index above 102.4.

Wednesday’s U.S. inflation report is the week’s key macroeconomic event. Annual core inflation is expected to come in at 2.5%, while headline inflation is forecast at 3.7%, which would mark a reacceleration from the previous month.

IREN IREN$34.83·Market Closed, which has repurposed from bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure, has secured a multiyear cloud services agreement with artificial intelligence firm Anthropic, according to The Information. IREN shares are up 4% pre-market.

title: MEXC Brings AI, TradFi and the Future of Trading to Life at TOKEN2049 Singapore
summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 12, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, concluded its TOKEN2049 Singapore presence with a series of interactive experiences and industry discussions spanning TradFi access, AI-powered trading and the future evolution of global trading platforms. MEXC’s ...
content:
Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 12, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, concluded its TOKEN2049 Singapore presence with a series of interactive experiences and industry discussions spanning TradFi access, AI-powered trading and the future evolution of global trading platforms.

MEXC’s presence centered on three key areas: the MEXC Stage and a panel featuring MEXC CEO Vugar Usi Zade and Payward Co-CEO Arjun Sethi, hands-on AI experiences including the MEXC AI Trading Challenge powered by MEXC CLI and the AI Bond Test, and The NEXT Newspaper, an interactive experience that brought insights around TradFi, AI and the future of investing into a more engaging community format.

Thousands of participants joined MEXC’s on-site activities during the event, reflecting strong interest in both AI-enabled trading and broader access to traditional financial markets. Across the booth and the MEXC Stage, these themes came together around a broader question: how trading platforms can become more connected, accessible and intelligent as crypto and traditional finance continue to converge.

Exploring AI Through Hands-On Experiences

AI was one of the most visible themes across the MEXC booth.

Through the MEXC AI Trading Challenge, visitors experienced how natural-language instructions, AI agents and MEXC CLI can work together to move trading ideas more directly from analysis to action. The experience demonstrated how users can express what they want to do in everyday language, while AI agents supported by MEXC CLI connect those intentions with MEXC trading capabilities.

Alongside the trading experience, the AI Bond Test offered a more playful way for visitors to explore their relationship with AI, including how they use, trust and interact with AI in everyday decision-making.

Together, the two activities reflected growing interest not only in AI as an information or research tool, but also in how it could become a more natural part of the broader trading experience.

Bringing TradFi Insights Into the Community

Traditional financial markets were another major area of interest at TOKEN2049.

Through The NEXT Newspaper, MEXC transformed research insights around AI, trading and global markets into an interactive experience. Visitors could personalize their own newspaper with their photo and predictions about the future of investing, creating a bridge between research, market trends and community participation.

The activation reflected a broader shift in retail investing as users increasingly look beyond crypto toward stocks, commodities and other traditional financial assets, while expecting to access these opportunities through more seamless digital platforms.

From Crypto-TradFi Convergence to Platform Collaboration

These themes also extended to the MEXC Stage, where MEXC CEO Vugar Usi Zade joined Payward Co-CEO Arjun Sethi.

The panel explored how crypto and traditional finance are moving toward a more connected, always-on financial environment, and how retail demand could help drive the evolution toward platforms that provide access across multiple asset classes.

Arjun highlighted the infrastructure needed to support this evolution, noting that the promise of 24/7 markets ultimately depends on connecting assets and collateral more effectively.

Collaboration was another key theme. Arjun pointed to partnerships as an important part of reaching more global users, specifically referencing MEXC as an example of a platform that could help partners succeed in their respective core markets. Vugar similarly highlighted how platforms can build on different strengths across infrastructure, market access and retail distribution rather than approaching every opportunity purely through competition.

AI also featured in the discussion as part of the longer-term evolution of trading. Vugar noted that AI can help retail users process large amounts of information more efficiently and convert insights into action, while increasingly agentic tools could further change how users interact with financial platforms.

From hands-on AI experiences to TradFi engagement and conversations about the future of market infrastructure, MEXC’s TOKEN2049 presence reflected a broader direction for trading: more connected markets, broader access and increasingly intelligent ways for users to participate.

For more highlights from TOKEN2049 Singapore, watch the event recap video.

About MEXC

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

Disclaimer

  • MH Markets wins Best CFD Broker in Asia Pacific 2026 at iFX EXPO Asia.

MH Markets was honored with the “Best CFD Broker in Asia Pacific 2026” award during iFX EXPO Asia. This recognition reflects the company’s continued commitment to the forex and CFD industry over the years, further affirming its strategic focus on expanding across Asian markets and advancing localized operations.

Asia is home to diverse trading needs and service environments. MH Markets continues to combine global resources with the market expertise of its regional teams to strengthen its service ecosystem in areas such as client communication, partner support, and trading education. This award marks an important milestone in the company’s regional development and reinforces its commitment to continuously enhancing service quality and building long-term relationships with clients and partners.

On the second day of the event, Khaled El Khatib, Head of Global Market Analystsat MH Markets, moderated a panel discussion titled “From Bitcoin to Gold: Where Does the Real Revenue Come From?” Together with industry representatives from B2BPrime, IC, ACCM, Bitget Academy, and GoldZip, the panel explored revenue models, customer acquisition costs, and compliance challenges in gold and cryptocurrency businesses. The discussion also covered gold tokenization, the convergence of traditional finance and blockchain technology, and potential directions for profitable growth over the next three years.

Building on this recognition, MH Markets will further refine its client service processes and cross-team collaboration to improve response times and issue resolution efficiency. In partner services, the company will continue to optimize marketing resources, educational content, and event support according to the needs of different regional markets, helping partners strengthen local market engagement and establish a more stable foundation for cooperation.

Meanwhile, MH Markets will continue to enhance its promotional campaigns and client reward programs, with a focus on accessibility, transparent rules, and customer experience. The latest MH Markets Global Trading Competition will also strengthen the brand’s engagement with trading communities worldwide. Through practical trading activities, market discussions, and experience sharing, the competition aims to broaden participation in trading education and deepen traders’ understanding of strategy application and risk management.

Looking ahead, MH Markets will continue to expand its global presence by combining localized services with global resources, further improving its products and service offerings, and deepening collaboration with partners across different markets to deliver an enhanced trading experience for traders worldwide.

title: Global financial watchdog calls for cross-border information sharing, planning for stablecoin crisis
summary: Coins jointly issued by multiple companies can trap reserves in one jurisdiction while redemption demands hit another, complicating cross-border crisis response.
content:
Oct 12, 2026, 7:02 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • The FSB warned global stablecoins and national rules remain untested in severe market crises, risking redemption and reserve delays.
  • The watchdog called for more cross-border information sharing, monitoring and planning for distress or failure in the fiat-pegged tokens.
  • Multi-issuer models can trap reserves in one jurisdiction while redemption demands hit another, complicating cross-border crisis response, while 24/7 trading and pseudonymous transactions increase systemic shock risks, it said.

The Financial Stability Board (FSB) warned that stablecoins could expose gaps in cross-border financial rules during a market crisis and remain untested in such a scenario, and called for more cross-border information sharing, monitoring and planning for stablecoin distress or failure.

The G20’s financial watchdog said in a report that global stablecoins, crypto tokens whose value is pegged to a fiat currency, have not been tested under severe stress or insolvency, while the national regulatory frameworks are developing at different speeds, raising questions over how holders would recover their funds if an issuer went under.

The stablecoin market started 2025 at around $206 billion in capitalization, and has grown to $306 billion. Most of that value is in stablecoins pegged to the U.S. dollar. While much of the value is used mainly to move in and out of crypto investments, the coins could eventually enable faster, cheaper payments, including across borders, the FSB said.

“Global stablecoin arrangements are inherently cross-border, yet national regulations are taking shape at different speeds and cross-border cooperation in this area is still in its infancy,” Chair Andrew Bailey wrote in an accompanying letter.

The report points to higher risks in so-called multi-issuer structures. Affiliated companies can issue the same stablecoin and share liability for it while keeping reserve assets in separate jurisdictions.

If holders can redeem with any issuer in the group, demand could pile up on a single entity, while the needed assets sit elsewhere. Moving those reserves may become harder during a crisis, the FSB warned. Legal claims could also become unclear if an issuer fails, as it It may be difficult to determine which country’s insolvency rules would apply.

Stablecoins can trade around the clock, while the markets for assets backing them have set operating hours. That mismatch could matter during a run because if redemptions cannot keep pace with selling, a token may lose its peg, the report added.

However, the FSB noted that deep, liquid secondary markets could also help pull a token back toward its peg through arbitrage.

Forced reserve sales and bank deposit withdrawals could then spread the shock into traditional financial markets as investors scramble for liquidity.

The FSB also pointed to weak data as a problem, as the pseudonymous nature of cryptocurrency transactions can make it hard to tell where holders are based and which jurisdiction applies.

The FSB called for more cross-border information sharing, monitoring and planning for stablecoin distress or failure. Its recommendations are not legally binding, but members tend to commit to putting agreed standards into practice nationally.

Bailey, who also serves as the governor of the Bank of England, has in the past warned international stablecoin rulemaking stalled. The FSB’s report comes just days ahead of the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors’ Oct. 15 meeting.

title: cTrader wins Best Trading Platform as Spotware puts broker growth in focus at iFX EXPO Asia
summary: The recognition comes as cTrader continues to strengthen its presence across key Asian markets, including mainland China, where the platform is specifically localised for traders in this region. content:
2026-10-12T13:00:34.573+02:00

Monday, 12/10/2026 | 11:00 GMT by cTrader

Disclaimer

  • cTrader has been named Best Trading Platform at UF Awards APAC 2026 during iFX EXPO Asia in Hong Kong.

The recognition comes as cTrader continues to strengthen its presence across key Asian markets, including mainland China, where the platform is specifically localised for traders in this region. Globally, more than 12 million traders already use cTrader, which supports 23 languages and serves more than 300 brokers and prop firms.

AI is high on the agenda for traders and brokers alike, and cTrader is already set up for it. cTrader MCP servers for trading connect the platform to popular AI apps. Traders state what they need in plain language, and the AI analyses markets, manages accounts, handles orders and positions or adjusts the trading workspace. In the meantime, with cTrader CLI, trading, account and algo operations can be managed from the command line manually or handed over to an AI assistant.

cTrader remains a best-in-class platform for traders at every stage of experience. Newer traders are drawn to the mobile-first, intuitive interface, built-in risk management tools, executable signals, price alerts and educational content. Experienced traders get the advanced order controls, a professional technical analysis workspace, native C# and Python support and free 24/7 cloud execution for cBots, with no VPS required.

What brokers asked us in Hong Kong and what we showed them

Three questions came up at the Expo: “How can we acquire new clients without extra spending?”, “What can we offer that competitors don’t?” and “How can we improve the cost-efficiency of our liquidity setup?”.

Here’s how we answered them.

Getting clients without paying for every click

The cTrader Leads programme helps brokers reach and convert traders who are already actively exploring broker offerings or looking for new trading tools within cTrader, at no upfront cost. Those opportunities come through cTrader Store and the cross-broker cTrader app, which together attract more than 170K visits per month. After conversion, the average first deposit reaches $800, with an average of 2.3 deposits per user per month.

Standing out in a crowded market

In an industry this competitive, differentiation has become a business priority. Multi-platform plugins open up a new opportunity for brokers and prop firms, letting them shape their cTrader offering around client needs, business goals and brand identity. A firm can build its own tools and services into cTrader, pre-install them for its clients and, optionally, list them in cTrader Store to reach new potential clients.

There is no need to wait for a core platform release. Brokers and prop firms can launch exclusive services on their own timelines, serve different trader segments and use cases and build an offering that is distinctly their own.

Making liquidity more cost-effective

Liquidity was another major topic in Hong Kong, in particular the pressure to improve pricing and execution without letting infrastructure costs rise at the same pace.

cFinancial, an institutional liquidity provider for brokers and prop firms, was present at the expo and drew particularly strong interest. Ricardo Dias, Business Development Manager, even called it “the star of the Expo.” cFinancial offers executable pricing, intelligent routing and resilient infrastructure, with a flat commission of $4 per $1M on FX and metals.

For brokers, however, the challenge does not end with accessing liquidity. Once it is connected, they also need an efficient way to manage aggregation, routing and exposure. This is the role of cBridge, a standalone liquidity bridge, which brings these functions into a single workflow across cTrader, MT4, MT5 and FIX API. With fixed, infrastructure-based pricing, bridge costs do not rise with trading volume, offering potential savings of up to 80% compared with volume-based models.

Taken together, cFinancial and cBridge cover both sides of the equation: access to competitive liquidity and the cost-efficient infrastructure needed to manage it.

Get in touch with our team

The Expo may be over, but the challenges raised there are as relevant as ever. If you could not be in Hong Kong, we would be happy to talk you through the solutions that will fit your business best.

Spotware Systems is a leading fintech company founded in 2010, based in Limassol, Cyprus, with a global team of 200+ professionals. It designs and delivers innovative trading technology and custom solutions for brokers worldwide, supporting long-term growth and scalability. Spotware’s solutions include cTrader, the flagship trading platform, and cBridge, a standalone, fixed-price liquidity bridge for all platforms. Spotware’s expertise is consistently recognised with multiple international industry awards, including Best Trading Platform, Best Services for Partners and Best Mobile Trading App.

Taking advantage of the gathering, HTX pursued a multifaceted approach encompassing global industry engagement, ecosystem development, ...
